title: Expand responsive visual and accessibility release gates
description:
## Outcome
Turn responsive, overlap, maximum-content, zoom and route-level accessibility expectations into deterministic release gates so future frontend work cannot reintroduce the defects found by the audit.

## Scope
Expand Playwright projects/helpers/specs and fixtures to cover landing, `/science` and critical `/lab` states; add page overflow and element-overlap geometry checks; add 320 and representative tablet coverage while retaining 360/desktop baselines; add maximum-content and 200% zoom/reflow checks; cover keyboard, touch, reduced motion and no-JavaScript critical content; integrate axe, Lighthouse, static-output and bundle evidence into the single release command; document snapshot review protocol and prove the agent handoff contract on one completed child.

## Non-goals
No visual design change, arbitrary screenshot increase for every permutation, flaky pixel assertion, hidden test exclusion, browser matrix expansion without risk value, threshold relaxation, production analytics or replacement of manual spot checks explicitly required by WCAG/release docs.

## Stop condition
A test that cannot distinguish a real regression from unstable timing/font/data must be made deterministic or removed in favor of a stable semantic/geometry assertion. Do not widen tolerances, add retries or mask regions solely to make it green.
design: Keep a small screenshot set for visually meaningful route/state combinations and use semantic/geometry assertions for the full matrix. Freeze locale, timezone, color scheme, reduced motion, viewport and fixture data. Add helpers for page width, pairwise non-intersection, viewport containment, minimum target size and evidence visibility. Production static output is the release authority; dev-server screenshots are diagnostic only.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `pnpm release:check` runs production-static checks for landing, `/science` and selected/unselected `/lab` at desktop, 360 mobile and targeted 320/tablet geometry projects without a separate undocumented command.
2. Overflow assertions run on every route/state; a shared helper asserts pairwise non-intersection of rendered **text line boxes** (`Range.getClientRects()`, not element bounding boxes) for marker/headline, navigation, card metric/caveat and drawer/control pairs; failures print locators and measured rectangles. The helper reproduces the F-1 failure on the pre-fix commit and must exclude the three documented false-positive classes: `position: fixed` elements measured against scrolled-past content, stale rects under `content-visibility: hidden`, and union boxes of wrapped inline elements.
3. Maximum-content fixtures and 200% zoom checks cover long Unicode identity/context, longest metric/caveat/source copy and all uncertainty states without modifying production artifacts; the fixtures from scoutlens-uze.7 are wired into the matrix.
4. Visual baselines include landing, How-it-works orientation/result and critical Lab fingerprint/retrieval/neighbor/challenge states; every accepted update has an intended-difference manifest.
5. Axe reports no serious/critical violation across routes/open dialog; keyboard, touch, reduced-motion and no-JavaScript critical-content flows are automated where deterministic. When a modal dialog is open, geometry scans are scoped to the dialog subtree and the dialog's own containment is asserted separately, because top-layer content does not affect page `scrollWidth`.
6. Lighthouse, INP proxy, static transfer, CSS and JavaScript budgets remain unchanged; `scoutlens-jtt.14` records at least 20 KiB initial-JS headroom before final gate closure.
7. A handoff drill using one completed frontend child demonstrates that allowed files, stop condition, screenshots and commands were sufficient; closure notes map every QA-audit matrix cell in `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` section 2 to an automated gate or a named manual release check, including the rows marked BLOCKED.

## scoutlens-uze.1 coverage map (2026-08-04, commit b28b921)

Full report: `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` section 5.

| Gate | Covers today | Gap this bead must close |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/visual.spec.ts` | 2 screenshots of `/lab` (`retrieval-neighbors`, `neighbor-cards`) at 360 and 1280 | Landing and `/science` have **no** visual baseline at all, so F-1 is invisible to CI. No 320, no tablet, no zoom, no error state, no drawer, no maximum content |
| `e2e/core-flow.spec.ts` | Keyboard flow + `expectNoPageOverflow` on `/lab` at 360 and 1280 | Page overflow is not asserted on `/` or `/science`; text-collision geometry is asserted nowhere; 320 and 200% zoom absent |
| `e2e/quality-contract.spec.ts` | axe on 3 routes + open drawer; local-link crawl; cache headers | No axe on empty-filter, failure or maximum-content states; no 320 or zoom projects |
| `e2e/failure-states.spec.ts` | 4 failure fixtures, `test.skip` on non-desktop | Runs at 1280 only — no responsive assertion on any failure state |
| `lighthouserc.json` | `/lab/` x3 at mobile 360 | Landing and `/science` are unmeasured |
| `scripts/check-static-output.mjs` | Route + landmark presence in the export | Never exercises the unknown-route path (see scoutlens-uze.8) |
| `scripts/check-budgets.mjs` | gzip budgets | n/a |

**Uncovered critical cells to assign to gates:** `/science` at 320/360/768 and 640x512 (would catch F-1); text line-box collision on all routes; page overflow and viewport containment on landing and `/science`; a 320 px Playwright project; failure and maximum-content states at mobile widths; the unknown-route response.

**Reusable helper the audit harness proved.** `web/test-results/frontend-qa-audit/audit.mjs` (gitignored, disposable) contains working implementations of the eight measurement dimensions, including the two that need care:
- **Text collision must use `Range.getClientRects()` line boxes, not `getBoundingClientRect()`.** F-1 is invisible to an element-box assertion because the marker is a stretched, clipped grid item. See scoutlens-uze.4.
- **A modal `<dialog>` lives in the top layer**, so a naive pairwise overlap scan reports every element behind it. Scope the scan to the dialog subtree when one is open, and measure the dialog's own geometry separately (page `scrollWidth` does not grow with top-layer content).

**Known false positives to filter, with their causes:** `position: fixed` elements compared against scrolled-past content in viewport coordinates (`.skip-link`); stale rects inside `content-visibility: hidden` subtrees (collapsed `<details>`); union boxes of wrapped inline elements (two links in one paragraph). All three appeared in the audit and are documented in the report's "Measurement artifacts" section.

**Baseline the new gates should lock in** (measured across 93 cells / 16 states / 8 viewports): 0 page-overflow failures, 0 viewport-edge crossings outside declared scrollers, 100% of tab stops with a visible focus indicator, 0 horizontally clipped focus stops, 0 serious/critical axe violations in 55 audited cells, 0 JavaScript page errors, exactly 1 CSS animation and 0 CSS transitions site-wide with `prefers-reduced-motion` correctly honoured.

**Blocked matrix cells** are owned by scoutlens-uze.7 and must be wired into these gates once that lands.

title: Harden the complete Lab mobile information hierarchy
description:
## Outcome
Make the complete Lab journey usable on narrow screens and under maximum content after uncertainty and the identity challenge land, without hiding evidence or changing any analytical behavior.

## Scope
Implement the frozen mobile content order for selector/results, selected-profile context, identity challenge/retrieval, fingerprint, uncertainty/evidence rail, neighbors/drawer and 32-value table; reduce initial cognitive load through accessible progressive disclosure; harden filters, toggles, cards, labels, long names, multi-team context, interval/rank copy, comparison drawer and internal tables; preserve direct URL and desktop information density; cover all failure and uncertainty states.

## Non-goals
No new metric, rank, neighbor, uncertainty calculation, recommendation workflow, scientific copy/value change, search behavior change, desktop feature removal, inaccessible collapsed content, horizontal page scroll, or performance-budget relaxation.

## Stop condition
If the required mobile order conflicts with DOM semantics, focus order, no-JavaScript evidence or the frozen identity/uncertainty contract, stop and resolve the owning contract; do not use CSS visual reordering that leaves assistive technology in a different sequence.
design: Use semantic DOM order, not `order`-only visual rearrangement, for the accepted mobile hierarchy. Advanced tables may use labeled internal horizontal scrolling and accessible disclosure but all point estimates, uncertainty state, caveats and text equivalents remain reachable. Preserve Python-provided ordering and direct profile URL. The comparison dialog keeps focus trap/return and query context. Work only after the new identity and uncertainty surfaces are stable.
acceptance_criteria:
1. At 320/360/375 px, the Lab follows the accepted mobile narrative order and a user can select a profile, complete/revisit the identity flow, inspect fingerprint/uncertainty, open/close a neighbor and reach the full table without losing query context.
2. Selected/unselected, zero-filter, unknown-key, missing-artifact, incompatible-schema and pending/available/insufficient uncertainty states have no overlap, clipping, page overflow or unreachable recovery action.
3. Long Unicode names, multi-team contexts, longest competition/feature/caveat labels and widest valid intervals/ranks render in maximum-content fixtures without changing or truncating essential meaning.
4. Fingerprint and uncertainty graphics have text equivalents; the 32-value and contribution tables use labeled/focusable internal scrolling rather than expanding page width. Additionally, the feature-name row header stays readable while the table is scrolled to its far-right column: assert at 320, 360 and 1280 CSS pixels that after setting `.fingerprint-table-scroll.scrollLeft = scrollWidth`, the `th[scope="row"]` ink box is still within the scroller's client box. Measured today: ratio 5.75x at 320 px with 1,216 px hidden and `position: static` on the row header, so this assertion currently fails.
5. Keyboard focus order matches semantic/visual order, dialog focus trap and return remain correct, touch targets meet 44 px and reduced motion preserves all analytical meaning. Current dialog behaviour (focus on `Close comparison` at open, return to the invoking button on `Escape`) is already correct and must not regress.
6. Desktop 1024/1280/1440 behavior and information density remain equivalent; stored ordering, direct URLs, filter semantics and artifact values are unchanged.
7. Unit, E2E, mobile/desktop visual, axe, static-output, interaction-latency and transfer/bundle gates pass with no scientific or generated-artifact diff. Baseline to hold: 0 page-overflow failures and 0 serious/critical axe violations across every audited Lab state.

## scoutlens-uze.1 audit evidence (2026-08-04, commit b28b921)

Full report: `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` section F-3 and section 4. Raw data: `web/test-results/frontend-qa-audit/`.

**F-3 — the 32-feature value table loses row identity while scrolling (Medium).**
`.fingerprint-value-table` carries a fixed `min-width: 1472px`, so `.fingerprint-table-scroll` scrolls horizontally at **every** viewport:

| Viewport | 320 | 360 | 375 | 768 | 1024 | 1280 | 1440 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| scrollWidth / clientWidth | 5.75x | 4.97x | 4.73x | 2.16x | 1.62x | 1.40x | 1.40x |

At 320 px, 1,216 px of 1,472 px are off-screen. The `th[scope="row"]` carrying the feature name is 272 px wide and `position: static`, so scrolling to `A global z`, `B global z`, `A/B support` or `Uncertainty` removes the only row identifier and the cells cannot be attributed.

Reproduce on `/lab/` at 320x800:
```js
const s = document.querySelector('.fingerprint-table-scroll');
const th = document.querySelector(".fingerprint-value-table tbody th[scope='row']");
({ ratio: s.scrollWidth / s.clientWidth, hidden: s.scrollWidth - s.clientWidth, rowHeader: getComputedStyle(th).position })
```
Observed `{ ratio: 5.75, hidden: 1216, rowHeader: 'static' }`.

**Compliance and usability were judged separately.** Labelling passes: the container is `role="region"`, `aria-label="Scrollable 32-feature value table"`, `tabindex="0"` at every viewport, and WCAG 1.4.10 exempts data tables from the no-horizontal-scroll requirement. The same holds for `.neighbor-drawer__table-scroll` (768 px content). This is a usability defect, not a conformance failure — do not "fix" it by removing the scroller or hiding columns.

**Lab state already clean at 320/360/375/768/1280 and 200% zoom — do not regress.** Zero page overflow and zero viewport-edge crossings in every Lab state audited: default, selected, empty filters, active filters, unknown profile, missing artifact, checksum mismatch, open comparison drawer, stored maximum content (`wy-25999-c-412`), synthetic maximum content, and synthetic uncertainty `available` / `insufficient`. Zero serious/critical axe violations. Tab-stop counts stable per state across all viewports (lab 38, drawer 45, unknown profile 29, missing/incompatible artifact 30).

**Comparison drawer already meets the release protocol.** `Enter` on a neighbor opens the native `<dialog>` with focus on `Close comparison`; `Escape` closes it and returns focus to the invoking `Open evidence comparison` button. The dialog never exceeds the viewport (full-bleed <= 768 px, 832 px wide above) and introduces no overflow of its own.

**Maximum content available today.** Longest published values: display name `K. Théophile Catherine` (22 chars), team join `Saint-Étienne / Olympique Marseille` (35 chars), at most 2 teams per period, competition `Spanish first division` (22 chars). All 1,257 profiles are `uncertainty_status: "pending"`. Anything beyond that requires the fixtures in scoutlens-uze.7.

**Touch targets inside the Lab.** Only shared-shell navigation (owned by scoutlens-uze.4) and in-sentence links fall below 44x44; Lab controls, filters, selects, profile result buttons and neighbor buttons already meet it. `.lab-evidence-rail a` (223x15) and `.retrieval-boundary a` (207x38 at 320 px) are the two Lab-owned links below the bar.

title: Repair shared shell, landing and Science responsiveness
description:
## Outcome
Repair the shared shell, landing and current `/science` responsive baseline so headings, markers, navigation, cards, metrics, caveats and provenance remain legible and operable at narrow widths and zoom before new narrative components are added.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build/serve the current static web application with the pinned commands.
2. Open `/science` at 320 or 360 CSS pixels.
3. Inspect the first dark experiment card: the `01 · question` marker and `Can an event profile identify a player?` heading occupy intersecting visual space.
4. Repeat route inspection with long source/caveat text and 200% zoom; note that current visual regression does not cover landing or `/science`, so the defect is not release-blocking today.

## Scope
Fix the reproduced marker/title collision, navigation wrapping/spacing, hero and page-heading scale, grid collapse, card/content wrapping, metric/evidence links, provenance disclosures, long source/caveat copy, focus/touch behavior and shared containers on landing and `/science`; cover 320 through 1440 px and 200% zoom; add targeted regression assertions and route screenshots.

## Non-goals
No How-it-works content rewrite, identity challenge, Lab information-architecture change, scientific copy/value modification, unrelated rebrand, desktop-only polish, hidden overflow as a fix, smaller-than-accessible text or relaxed screenshot/accessibility/performance thresholds.

## Stop condition
If a fix requires shortening scientific content, removing a caveat/source, changing semantic order or editing a denied file, stop and link the owning narrative/contract bead; presentation must adapt to content, not discard it.
design:
Work only in the allowlisted shared shell, landing/science presentation components, their owned style layers and named tests. Wrapping must use intrinsic sizing (`minmax(0, ...)`, `overflow-wrap`, flexible layout) rather than arbitrary clipping. At 200% zoom, validate reflow rather than relying only on viewport screenshots.

## Corrected assertion technique (scoutlens-uze.1, 2026-08-04)

The earlier plan — "assert that the `/science` step marker and heading **bounding boxes** do not intersect at 320/360 px" — would pass today while the defect is on screen, and must not be used.

Measured: `.frozen-question > .research-step__marker` is a grid item stretched by `align-items` to the full row height and clipped to its 40 px track, so `getBoundingClientRect()` returns `left 35 … right 75`, while `#frozen-question-heading` returns `left 91 …`. The boxes never intersect at any width. What collides is the rendered **text**: the marker wraps and its second line box reaches `right 96.2`.

The assertion must therefore compare `Range.getClientRects()` line boxes, pairwise, for the two elements — not their element boxes. The same helper should be reused by scoutlens-uze.6 for every route.

## Measured mechanism

`.frozen-question` is `grid-template-columns: 5rem minmax(0, 1fr)`, narrowed to `2.5rem minmax(0, 1fr)` with a `1rem` gap inside `@media (max-width: 48rem)` (globals.css:2510). The marker string `01 · question` has an intrinsic single-line width of 91 px; the word `question` alone measures 61.2 px against a 40 px track. It wraps and overshoots the track by 21.2 px, which exceeds the 16 px gap, leaving −5.2 px clearance.

Any fix must keep the marker string intact (it is derived from `narrative[0].kind`) — the track, the gap or the wrapping behaviour is what changes, not the content.
acceptance_criteria:
1. At every frozen viewport, header/wordmark/navigation, landing hero, claims, fingerprint preview, experiment cards and current science stages have no page overflow, essential clipping, unintended overlap or off-screen interactive control.
2. The `/science` `01 · question` marker and `#frozen-question-heading` never intersect. The assertion compares `Range.getClientRects()` **line boxes** pairwise, not element bounding boxes, and runs at 320, 360, 375, 640, 768 and 640x512 (200% zoom). It reproduces the current failure — measured clearance −5.2 px, intersections 5.2x14.8 px and 5.2x5.3 px, constant at every width from 320 to 768 — and passes after the fix with clearance >= 0 at every asserted width. 769 px and above already pass (+50.8 px) and must not regress.
3. Long provider names, evidence URLs, metric labels, caveats and the longest supported/unsupported claim wrap without changing text, shrinking below readable sizes or hiding behind ellipsis.
4. At 200% zoom, content reflows in logical reading order, focus rings remain visible, navigation remains operable and all touch targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels. Current measured state at 360 px: `.site-nav a` is 66x17 (Overview), 105x17 (Fingerprint Lab) and 55x17 (Science); `.wordmark` is 123x34; the header wraps to two rows at every width <= 768 px (110 px tall vs 80 px at 1280 px). Note that WCAG 2.5.8 AA already passes via the spacing exception (minimum centre-to-centre distance 60.5 px >= 24 px), so the 44x44 bar here is a deliberate AAA/ergonomics target, not a conformance fix; enlarge the hit area without changing the visual type scale. In-sentence links (`.evidence-links a` 77x19, `.source-grid a`, `.provenance-drawer__content a`) meet the 2.5.8 inline exception and are out of scope.
5. New mobile and desktop screenshots cover landing and `/science`; intended differences are enumerated per component and unrelated snapshot regions remain stable.
6. Axe has no serious/critical violations, keyboard and reduced-motion checks pass, and Lighthouse/static budgets remain at their existing thresholds. Baseline to hold: 0 serious and 0 critical axe violations across 55 audited cells on 2026-08-04, and 0 page-overflow failures in 93/93 cells.
7. Git diff is limited to named presentation/style/test files and contains no metric value, claim/caveat, artifact, schema, generated-contract or data-loader change.

## scoutlens-uze.1 audit evidence (2026-08-04, commit b28b921)

Full report: `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` sections F-1 and F-4. Raw data: `web/test-results/frontend-qa-audit/` (gitignored).

**F-1 failing range, measured at 13 widths.** Clearance between marker ink and heading ink is a constant −5.2 px at 320, 340, 360, 375, 400, 420, 480, 560, 640, 700, 766, 767 and 768 px. It becomes +50.8 px at 769 px and above. The boundary is exactly the `@media (max-width: 48rem)` block. The 640x512 (200% zoom of 1280x1024) cell fails, so this is also a zoom-reflow defect.

Reproduce on the production fixture:
```
cd web && pnpm build && node scripts/serve-static.mjs --port 4173
```
then at 360x800 on `/science/`:
```js
const ink = (el) => { const r = document.createRange(); r.selectNodeContents(el); return [...r.getClientRects()]; };
const m = ink(document.querySelector('.frozen-question > .research-step__marker'));
const h = ink(document.querySelector('#frozen-question-heading'));
({ markerInkRight: Math.max(...m.map(r => r.right)), headingInkLeft: Math.min(...h.map(r => r.left)) })
```
Expected `headingInkLeft >= markerInkRight`; observed 91 vs 96.2.

Screenshots: `screenshots/probe-frozen-question-{320,360,768,769,1280}.png`. Data: `probe2.json#markerInk`, `probe3.json#markerBoundary`.

**Not reproduced as originally described.** The seed wording says the marker and heading "occupy intersecting visual space" and proposed a bounding-box assertion. The visual collision is real; the *element boxes* do not intersect at any width. See the Design section.

**F-4 data.** `probe2.json#header`, `probe3.json#navSpacing`, `screenshots/probe-header-360.png`.

**Already clean on landing and /science — do not regress.** 0 page-overflow failures, 0 elements crossing the viewport edge outside declared scrollers, 100% of tab stops with a visible focus indicator (landing 38 stops, science 44, stable across all 8 viewports), 0 serious/critical axe violations, 0 JavaScript page errors.

**Dismissed measurement artifacts** (documented in the report so they are not re-filed): `.skip-link` apparent overlaps (it is `position: fixed` at `translateY(-69.56px)`, never focused during measurement); the collapsed provenance `<details>` apparently overlapping `.provenance-version` (stale rect under `content-visibility: hidden`; the screenshot shows a correct collapse); `Official repository` / `User Agreement` at 320 px (wrapped-inline union box, line boxes are disjoint).

title: Modularize frontend styles with zero intended visual change
description:
## Outcome
Replace the single high-collision stylesheet ownership surface with the frozen token/base/shared/route layering while preserving the exact rendered product and scientific semantics.

## Scope
Apply the CSS file/import/cascade map selected by the ownership decision; move selectors mechanically into single-owner layers; remove only proven duplicates/dead rules; preserve selector specificity and source order or document the equivalent; update imports and style tooling; run full existing desktop/mobile visual, unit, E2E, accessibility, static-build and budget gates; record before/after stylesheet and bundle bytes.

## Non-goals
No visual fix, spacing/color/type change, class rename for taste, component redesign, copy change, DOM reorder, CSS framework, CSS-in-JS migration, quality-threshold change or opportunistic cleanup outside the migration map.

## Stop condition
Any unexplained screenshot difference, computed layout difference, cascade-order conflict, route behavior change or bundle-budget regression stops the extraction. Revert the affected move or split it into an explicit visual-fix bead; do not approve the difference as part of a refactor.
design: Use the exact target file map and import order frozen in `docs/frontend-agent-contract.md`. Migrate in deterministic sections so each commit/diff chunk has one source and destination. `globals.css` may remain as the root import/true-global surface but must no longer contain route-owned selector blocks. Do not have another agent edit a style layer while this bead is active.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tokens, reset/base typography, shared shell/primitives, landing, science and Lab selectors each have one documented owner file/layer matching the frozen map in docs/frontend-agent-contract.md §4.1; no route block remains in the global catch-all.
2. A selector inventory accounts for every moved/removed rule; removed rules have search or coverage evidence and no duplicate live definition remains. The 22 dead blocks and the two partially dead shared selector lists named in the Notes are resolved explicitly, and the six runtime-composed variant classes are confirmed retained.
3. Rendering is proven unchanged by a byte-identical `getComputedStyle()` diff over every element on landing, /science and every /lab state in docs/frontend-qa-audit.md §2, at 320, 360, 768 and 1280 CSS pixels, captured before and after the split. Existing desktop and mobile screenshots additionally pass with no intended visual differences; platform raster noise stays within the unchanged 3% threshold and is documented separately from layout. A passing screenshot alone does not satisfy this criterion.
4. Landing, `/science` and selected/unselected `/lab` DOM structure, accessible names, tab order, static URLs and data rendering remain unchanged.
5. Production CSS bytes, initial route transfer and JavaScript gzip are measured before/after; none exceeds its current value by more than measurement noise or any frozen budget. The dead-rule deletion should reduce CSS bytes by roughly 2,839 raw bytes; report the actual gzip delta.
6. `pnpm quality` and `pnpm release:check` pass without snapshot bulk regeneration, threshold edits, scientific artifact/schema changes or unrelated formatting churn.
7. Closure notes provide the final file ownership map and identify which files later landing/science and Lab agents may edit without overlap. Defect F-1 still reproduces identically after the split, confirming the pass was mechanical.
notes:
## Frozen inputs from scoutlens-uze.2 (2026-08-04)

Authority: `docs/frontend-agent-contract.md` §4. Decision record: D033. The analysis below is already done — do not redo it, but do verify it.

**Eight files, this cascade order, exact block counts (sum to the current 400):**
tokens 2 · base 13 · primitives 22 · shell 17 · research-story 79 · landing 21 · science 18 · lab 206 · (22 deleted, see below).

**Two placements that are not obvious.**
- `:root` appears **twice**: line 1 and again inside `@media (max-width: 48rem)` at line 2447 (`--shell` override). Both go to `tokens.css`, in that order.
- `research-story.css` is component-named, not route-named, because `research-story.tsx` renders on both landing and `/science`. A route-named split would give two beads a claim on the same 79 rules.
- `lab.css` stays as one 206-rule file. A three-way split was measured and rejected: 11 selector lists span two or three of the proposed sub-files (lines 1122, 1135, 1143, 1150, 1798, 2533, 2545, 2551, 2568, 2574, 2588), so splitting would duplicate and reorder declarations in the one pass that must not change rendering.

**Reorder safety, already checked.** A per-owner split cannot preserve global source order because ownership interleaves (lab occupies 1091–2441 while landing/science/research-story scatter from 165 to 2518). A reorder only changes rendering when two rules can match the same element, declare the same property and have equal specificity, and the split flips their order. Static analysis over all **473 selectors** under this order found **0 such pairs** and **0 unassigned selectors**. Treat that as a strong prior, not a proof — it approximates co-matching via ancestor-chain compatibility and does not model runtime class composition.

**Dead rules to delete, not move — 22 blocks, 2,839 bytes, 5.6% of the file.**
`.metric-grid`, `.metric-card`, `.metric-card__value`, `.metric-card h3`, `.metric-card > p:last-child`, `.principle`, `.principle > p`, `.lab-frame`, `.lab-frame__status`, `.status-dot`, `.step-list`, `.step-list li`, `.boundary-note`, `.boundary-note h2`, `.boundary-note p`, `.research-arc`, `.research-step`, `.research-step h2`, `.research-step p:last-child`, plus their own entries in the two media blocks.

**Two traps — partially dead shared selector lists. Split, do not delete whole.**
- Line 419 `.step-list span, .research-step__marker` — only `.step-list span` is dead. `.research-step__marker` is the live `/science` marker that defect F-1 (scoutlens-uze.4) depends on; it belongs in `science.css`.
- Line 2488 `@media (max-width: 48rem)` group `.metric-grid, .step-list, .experiment-grid, .experiment-grid--three` — both `.experiment-grid` halves are live and belong in `research-story.css`.

**Live despite looking unreferenced.** `.experiment-card--signal`, `.experiment-card--warning`, `.caveat--critical`, `.research-stage--warning`, `.lab-state--integrity`, `.lab-state--incompatible-data` are composed at runtime through template literals (`experiment-card--${emphasis}`, `lab-state--${problem.kind}`). A plain grep says 0 references. Do not delete them, and make any dead-CSS check account for dynamic composition.

**Extraction rules (contract §4.2).** Intra-layer source order preserved verbatim; media queries distributed into their owning layer at the end of that file with the `64rem` block before the `48rem` block; no declaration edited, added, removed or reformatted; no `@layer`, no `:where()`, no specificity rewriting.

**Verification.** A screenshot comparison cannot see a sub-pixel cascade change inside the 3% `maxDiffPixelRatio`. The binding proof is a `getComputedStyle()` snapshot over every element on every route and audited state, before and after, diffed byte-for-byte. The state/viewport list is `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` §2.

**Known pre-existing defect — do not fix here.** F-1 (the `/science` marker collision at ≤768 px) is present before and after this bead and stays present; it is owned by scoutlens-uze.4. If the computed-style diff is clean, F-1 must still reproduce identically afterwards. That is a useful positive control.

title: Freeze the delegated frontend ownership and delivery contract
description:
## Outcome
Freeze a file-level delegation and delivery contract so a specialist frontend agent can execute a ready bead independently without authority to change scientific semantics, data outputs or release thresholds.

## Scope
Define allowlist, conditional-review list and denylist by directory/file class; assign ownership for content, components, styles, tests, artifacts and generated code; freeze one-bead/branch/PR protocol; define reproduction and evidence template; define screenshot-update policy, overlapping-work exclusion, cross-boundary escalation, allowed commands, clean-worktree checks and Definition-of-Done handoff; select the CSS layering/file map used by the mechanical extraction task.

## Non-goals
No frontend implementation, repository-wide agent policy rewrite, automatic commit/push permission, scientific reviewer replacement, framework migration, blanket permission to edit `web/src/content/**`, or exception based only on a task being visually motivated.

## Rationale
The current presentation code and 2,651-line global stylesheet mix shared and route concerns. Explicit authority and file ownership are required before parallel delegation; otherwise a visual task can silently alter claims, artifacts or another agent's work.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Let each agent infer ownership from the task: rejected because the user explicitly requires low-interpretation, confidence-preserving handoff.
2. Deny all component/content changes and allow CSS only: rejected because responsive hierarchy and accessibility sometimes require semantic markup changes.
3. Permit all `web/**`: rejected because generated contracts, artifact copies and evidence-loading code are scientifically sensitive.
4. Complete a wholesale design-system rewrite first: rejected as unnecessary scope and portfolio delay.

## Stop condition
Any requested edit outside the task allowlist, any overlapping active bead on the same route/style layer, or any need to change a metric/caveat/evidence identifier stops implementation until a dependency or explicit owner review is recorded.
design: Create `docs/frontend-agent-contract.md` and a decision-log entry. Default allowlist: explicitly named route files under `web/src/app/**`, presentation components under `web/src/components/**`, route/shared style files selected by this decision and named `web/e2e/**` tests. Conditional list: `web/src/content/**`, package/build configuration and snapshot files, each requiring explicit issue scope. Denylist: `src/scoutlens/**`, `config/**`, `schemas/**`, `web/src/contracts/generated/**`, root or web `public/showcase/**`, `artifacts/**`, frozen science reports and metric/caveat/claim changes. Git commit, push, PR and Dolt sync remain governed by current user/repository authorization.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The contract contains an unambiguous allow/conditional/deny table with examples for every current frontend directory and names the reviewer/owning workstream for conditional changes.
2. A copy-pastable task handoff template requires issue ID, outcome, allowed files, forbidden files, reproduction, viewport/state matrix, acceptance commands, screenshots, scientific invariants, stop conditions and escalation path.
3. The delivery protocol freezes one bead/branch/PR, prohibits concurrent edits to the same route/style layer, preserves unrelated dirty-worktree changes and forbids commit/push/Dolt sync without current authority.
4. Snapshot policy requires an enumerated intended-difference list, before/after evidence and reviewer inspection; bulk baseline regeneration or tolerance increase is prohibited.
5. The decision selects an exact CSS target map and import/cascade order that separates tokens/base/shared shell/landing/science/lab ownership while preserving static Next.js behavior.
6. Three boundary scenarios are resolved explicitly: presentation-only component markup, evidence-loading/content change and generated-contract/artifact change; the latter always blocks frontend execution.
7. A dry-run handoff for the known `/science` overlap can be executed from the contract without an unstated file, behavior or quality decision, and the decision log records rejected alternatives.

title: Audit every public route across the responsive QA matrix
description:
## Outcome
Produce a reproducible, route-by-route defect inventory that separates page overflow, element overlap, clipping, poor mobile hierarchy, accessibility and performance risks before any responsive fix is attempted.

## Scope
Audit production-static landing, `/science` and `/lab` at 320, 360, 375, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 CSS pixels; cover selected/unselected, filters-empty, unknown profile, missing/incompatible artifact, pending/available/insufficient uncertainty and open neighbor/challenge states as they become available; test normal and maximum-content player/team/competition/copy fixtures, 200% zoom, keyboard traversal, reduced motion and light/dark behavior if supported; capture evidence and create/refine one bead per actionable defect.

## Non-goals
No CSS/component fix, snapshot acceptance, content rewrite, framework change, scientific output change, subjective redesign backlog or issue without reproducible route/state/viewport evidence.

## Known seed defects
Reproduce the <=360 px overlap between the `01 · question` marker and the first `/science` card heading; verify whether header navigation and long Lab cards remain usable below 360 px; record that current visual snapshots cover retrieval/neighbors but not landing or `/science`.

## Stop condition
If the production fixture cannot represent a required state, create the smallest deterministic fixture gap bead and mark that matrix cell blocked; do not substitute dev-only data or manually edited DOM content as closure evidence.
design: Create `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` as a dated evidence report, not the task source of truth. Each defect row names route, state, viewport/zoom, locator/component, screenshot/trace, expected behavior, observed behavior, severity, existing/new bead ID and owning workstream. Use the pinned production build/serve commands from `docs/flagship-quality-gates.md`. Store lasting automated baselines only in the existing Playwright structure; disposable screenshots remain test artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The audit matrix contains every required viewport, route and state with pass, reproducible defect bead or explicit fixture blocker; blank and subjective cells are not allowed.
2. Every recorded defect includes exact reproduction commands, route/query, viewport, browser/zoom, stable locator, screenshot or trace, expected/actual result, severity and owner.
3. The known `/science` marker/title overlap is reproduced at its failing widths and assigned to a specific repair bead with a geometry-based acceptance assertion.
4. Page scroll width, essential element bounding boxes, focus visibility/order, touch-target size, internal scroll labeling and 200% reflow are evaluated separately; passing one does not imply the others.
5. Maximum-content fixtures include long Unicode player and team names, multi-team context, longest metric/caveat copy and all uncertainty states without modifying production artifacts.
6. Existing Playwright/Lighthouse/axe coverage is mapped to the matrix, and each uncovered critical cell is assigned to the regression-gate bead.
7. No source/CSS snapshot is changed; closure notes list only evidence documents/test artifacts and newly created/refined Beads issues.
notes:
## Closure evidence (2026-08-04)

Deliverable: `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` (new, only file added to version control).
Harness and raw data: `web/test-results/frontend-qa-audit/` — gitignored, cleared by `playwright test`, regenerable via the commands in the report header.

**Environment.** Commit b28b921 on codex/deterministic-match-bootstrap. Build `cd web && pnpm build` (Next.js 16.2.12 static export). Server `node scripts/serve-static.mjs --port 4173` — the same fixture `pnpm release:check` uses. Chromium 151.0.7922.34 via @playwright/test 1.62.0.

**Deviation.** Node v24.18.0 against the pinned 24.14.x; pnpm 11.9.0 matched. `pnpm build` printed `Unsupported engine` and otherwise succeeded. Every finding is a geometry or DOM fact that does not depend on the Node patch level, but confirmation on the pinned Node is the correct follow-up before any fix is validated.

**Execution.** 93 cells = 16 states x 8 viewports (320, 360, 375, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 640x512 as 200% zoom), with edge/failure states swept at 320/360/768/1280/zoom200. Eight dimensions measured independently per cell (page scroll width; essential bounding boxes; text line-box collision; focus visibility/order; touch-target size; internal scroll labelling; 200% reflow; axe serious/critical).

### Acceptance criteria

1. **Every viewport/route/state has pass, defect bead or explicit blocker.** Report section 2 is the matrix; 93/93 cells carry a verdict, three cells are marked BLOCKED with a named owner, and section 4 records the verified passes so no cell rests on a subjective judgement.
2. **Every defect has commands, route, viewport, browser/zoom, locator, screenshot, expected/actual, severity, owner.** Report sections 3 and F-1..F-6; each defect carries a runnable console snippet, measured numbers and a bead id.
3. **The /science marker/title overlap is reproduced at its failing widths and assigned with a geometry acceptance assertion.** Reproduced at 320, 340, 360, 375, 400, 420, 480, 560, 640, 700, 766, 767 and 768 px with a constant −5.2 px clearance and 5.2x14.8 px / 5.2x5.3 px intersections; clears at 769 px (+50.8 px). Assigned to scoutlens-uze.4 with the corrected `Range.getClientRects()` line-box assertion. **Correction:** the seed described an element overlap. The element boxes never intersect at any width — the marker is a stretched, clipped grid item at `left 35 … right 75` — so the previously proposed bounding-box assertion would have passed while the defect was on screen. Only the rendered text collides. This is recorded in scoutlens-uze.4's Design and Notes.
4. **Six dimensions evaluated separately.** Page scroll width: 0 failures in 93/93. Bounding boxes: 0 viewport-edge crossings outside declared scrollers. Focus visibility/order: 100% of tab stops with a visible indicator, 0 horizontally clipped stops, stable stop counts per state across all viewports. Touch targets: measured and re-judged against WCAG 2.5.8 including the spacing exception (minimum centre distance 60.5 px, so AA passes; the 17 px navigation strip is filed on ergonomics/AAA). Internal scroll labelling: both scrollers pass role/name/tabindex at every viewport — recorded as a pass even though the same table is a usability defect under F-3. 200% reflow: dedicated 640x512 pass plus the 320 px column as the 400%-zoom equivalent. Passing one never marked another as passing.
5. **Maximum-content fixtures without modifying production artifacts.** Stored maximum measured from the published catalog: display name `K. Théophile Catherine` (22 chars), team join `Saint-Étienne / Olympique Marseille` (35 chars), 2 teams per period, `Spanish first division` (22 chars); audited via `/lab/?player=wy-25999-c-412`. Beyond that, a synthetic 40-char Unicode identity with two long club names, doubled caveat copy, plus `available` and `insufficient` uncertainty, was served through HTTP interception with a recomputed manifest sha256 — the same boundary technique as e2e/failure-states.spec.ts. No file under public/showcase/v1/ was touched. The two states the fixture genuinely cannot reach are marked BLOCKED and owned by scoutlens-uze.7.
6. **Existing coverage mapped; uncovered critical cells assigned.** Report section 5 maps all seven gates cell by cell. Headline gap: `e2e/visual.spec.ts` holds two /lab screenshots and no landing or /science baseline at all, so F-1 is invisible to CI. Assigned to scoutlens-uze.6, refined with the coverage table, the line-box helper requirement, the top-layer dialog caveat and the three false-positive classes to filter.
7. **No source or snapshot change.** `git status`: `docs/frontend-qa-audit.md` added; `.beads/*.jsonl` updated by bd. No file under web/src, web/e2e, web/scripts, public/, artifacts/, config/ or schemas/ modified; no visual snapshot regenerated. Unrelated: `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` gained a `fireworks-ai` dependency during the session from outside this task — not touched, flagged for the owner.

### Gates run

`pnpm build` PASS (includes assets:sync, TypeScript, static:check — "Static export contains all routes and semantic landmarks"). `pnpm lint` PASS. `pnpm typecheck` PASS. `pnpm contracts:check` PASS ("Generated TypeScript contract is current"). Full `pnpm release:check` was not run: it regenerates visual snapshots' comparison state and runs Lighthouse, neither of which this audit is allowed to change or needed.

### Beads

Created: scoutlens-uze.7 (fixture gap for the two blocked cells), scoutlens-uze.8 (unknown routes bypass the built 404 page), scoutlens-uze.9 (tabular numerals on the rank figure, color-scheme declaration).
Refined: scoutlens-uze.4 (F-1 corrected assertion + F-4 measured targets), scoutlens-uze.5 (F-3 scroll ratios + sticky row-header acceptance), scoutlens-uze.6 (coverage map + helper requirements).
Dependency added: scoutlens-uze.6 depends on scoutlens-uze.7.

### Risks

- Node patch-level deviation, above.
- `web/test-results/` is Playwright's `outputDir` and is cleared on the next `playwright test` run. The report is self-contained by design; the raw artifacts are regenerable, not durable.
- The three BLOCKED cells remain unaudited as published data until scoutlens-uze.7 lands.

Evidence report at docs/frontend-qa-audit.md; 6 defects filed (1 High, 3 Medium, 2 Low), 3 blocked cells assigned, existing gate coverage mapped. See closure notes for the criterion-by-criterion mapping. No source, style or snapshot file changed.

title: Validate public comprehension and claims consistency
description:
## Outcome
Prove that the completed public narrative is understandable, internally consistent and release-ready before it becomes the source for the portfolio case study.

## Scope
Execute the frozen 90-second comprehension checklist against the production build; run independent public-only reviews; verify claim, metric, source, season, limitation and AI-role consistency across landing, `/science`, `/lab`, README-facing copy and case-study inputs; audit direct links and no-JavaScript content; record deviations and create narrowly scoped defect beads rather than accepting ambiguous copy.

## Non-goals
No formal user-research or scout-validation study, new feature, visual redesign, metric selection after seeing feedback, promotional rewrite, silent snapshot update or release deployment.

## Stop condition
Any reviewer answer that requires repository knowledge, conflicts with the canonical answer, misses the strongest confound/data vintage, or infers recommendation/currentness blocks the gate and creates a defect assigned to the owning narrative or frontend bead.
design: Create `docs/public-understanding-check.md` containing the fixed prompts, canonical evidence-backed answers, timing protocol and result template. Run at least two independent reviews whose only input is the built public site; at least one reviewer must not be the implementation agent. Treat this as portfolio communication QA, not scientific validation. Use automated consistency assertions for everything machine-checkable and record human/model review only for comprehension and wording.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Two public-only reviewers complete the six-question checklist; each answer, elapsed time, ambiguity and evidence path is recorded, and at least one reviewer completes within 90 seconds without repository context.
2. Both reviewers identify the historical data vintage, supported claim, strongest team-context limitation, one unsupported claim and constrained AI role without being prompted toward the answer.
3. An automated audit verifies that every displayed metric/value/evidence link agrees across landing, `/science`, `/lab` and case-study inputs and originates in a versioned artifact.
4. Direct source, method, licence, artifact and decision links pass; no-JavaScript snapshots retain thesis, data vintage, supported/unsupported claims and provenance.
5. Forbidden-copy and currentness tests cover all public text; any necessary exception is evidence-linked and explicitly enumerated rather than regex-disabled globally.
6. Production unit, E2E, visual, accessibility, static-integrity and performance gates pass with frozen thresholds after all comprehension defects are closed.
7. Closure notes map every epic acceptance criterion to evidence and explicitly hand the accepted narrative/evidence paths to `scoutlens-jtt.7.3` without copying numeric constants.

title: Freeze the flagship identity-challenge contract
description:
## Outcome
Freeze a deterministic, implementation-ready identity-challenge interaction that turns the core temporal retrieval experiment into the flagship public moment without becoming a player quiz, recommendation game or client-side model.

## Scope
Choose the route/entry point, featured/default profile policy, exact user steps, information hidden before reveal, period-A query and period-B candidate explanation, baseline comparison, self-rank/retrieval reveal, contribution evidence, uncertainty/caveat placement, direct-link state, keyboard/touch behavior, no-JavaScript fallback, error states, analytics boundary and bundle budget.

## Non-goals
No implementation, random player-quality game, guessing football trivia, recomputing retrieval in JavaScript, user score/leaderboard, recommendation wording, live LLM dependency, new analytical output or choosing only favorable profiles without an editorial disclosure.

## Rationale
The existing Lab exposes the right evidence but begins as a dense dashboard. A guided reveal makes the scientific question concrete before presenting all controls, while deterministic artifacts and explicit caveats preserve trust.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Add more dashboard charts: rejected because it increases density without differentiating the product.
2. Make AI chat the primary interaction: rejected because AI would overshadow deterministic evidence and create a credential/runtime dependency.
3. Build a football-name trivia quiz: rejected because recognition skill is unrelated to the research question and encourages gamified quality interpretation.
4. Compute candidates live in the browser: rejected because Python artifacts are the sole scientific authority.

## Stop condition
If current showcase artifacts cannot support the frozen reveal, direct link, evidence decomposition or uncertainty state without browser recomputation, stop and create a narrowly scoped artifact-contract bead before implementation.
design: Create `docs/identity-challenge-contract.md` plus a decision-log entry. The contract must enumerate a state machine (`orientation`, `query`, `commit/reveal`, `evidence`, `degraded`), URL semantics, allowed artifact fields, event/copy names, focus transitions, responsive order and exact performance allocation. It must select one placement and reject alternatives so the implementation bead contains no product-design decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The contract selects one route/placement and specifies the complete state machine, default/featured profile policy, entry and exit CTAs, reload/share behavior and browser history behavior.
2. Each state lists visible/hidden fields, exact artifact owner, mandatory caveat/evidence IDs, uncertainty behavior and forbidden language; no state depends on hidden client computation.
3. The reveal explains candidate pool, same-player target, self-rank, baseline comparison and strongest contribution/disagreement without presenting a probability, quality score or recruitment result.
4. Keyboard order, focus movement, screen-reader announcements, 44 px touch targets, reduced motion, 320 px reading order and no-JavaScript fallback are specified as observable behaviors.
5. Unknown profile, missing artifact, checksum/schema mismatch, pending/insufficient uncertainty and loading states fail closed with recovery paths.
6. Initial-route and lazy-chunk gzip allocations are declared against existing budgets; analytics, if any, exclude search text, player identity history and persistent identifiers.
7. A decision-log entry records rationale, alternatives, chosen placement, editorial-selection disclosure and the exact dependencies that unblock implementation.

title: Implement the deterministic identity challenge
description:
## Outcome
Implement the frozen identity challenge as a shareable, deterministic and accessible flagship interaction whose reveal exactly reproduces stored retrieval, contribution, caveat and uncertainty evidence.

## Scope
Build the selected entry point and state machine; load only contract-approved showcase fields; preserve selected profile/query context; render query/reveal/evidence/degraded states; compare stored baseline and fingerprint outcomes; expose contribution and uncertainty evidence; implement keyboard, touch, reduced-motion, direct-link and no-JavaScript behavior; add unit, E2E, visual, accessibility and performance coverage.

## Non-goals
No browser-side ranking, cosine, neighbor or interval computation; no new experiment; no AI prose; no player-quality, style, recruitment or probability framing; no analytics beyond the frozen contract; no unrelated Lab redesign.

## Stop condition
Fail the build or render the typed degraded state when required identity, candidate-pool, evidence, caveat or uncertainty references are missing/incompatible. Never substitute catalog order, zero values, generic caveats or client recomputation.
design: Implement only after the identity contract, responsive baseline, uncertainty UI and JavaScript-headroom work are complete. Keep the deterministic static/no-credential experience authoritative. Non-critical reveal/evidence code must be lazy-loaded within the declared allocation. Component tests compare rendered values to production-format fixtures; E2E covers deep link, reload, back/forward, keyboard-only and narrow touch flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Orientation through evidence completion matches every state and transition in `docs/identity-challenge-contract.md`; invalid URL state returns to the documented recovery state without changing the scientific query.
2. Query identity/period, candidate count, self-rank, baseline outcome, cosine/contributions, uncertainty and caveats equal the selected stored artifact after declared display rounding.
3. Tests prove no ranking, similarity, nearest-neighbor, percentile or bootstrap calculation exists in the new client path and corrupt/missing evidence fails closed.
4. Keyboard and touch users can complete, revisit and exit the challenge; focus and announcements follow the contract; reduced motion and no-JavaScript states preserve the explanatory content.
5. Direct URLs reload and share deterministically, back/forward navigation is tested, and the editorial featured-profile choice is visibly disclosed.
6. 320/360/768/1280 screenshots show no overlap, clipping or page overflow; axe has no serious/critical violations; forbidden-language assertions pass.
7. `pnpm release:check` passes, initial and lazy JavaScript remain within frozen budgets with before/after gzip evidence, and no scientific artifact/schema/generated-contract diff is present.

title: Rebuild Science as a progressive How it works experience
description:
## Outcome
Turn the existing `/science` route into a progressive `How it works` experience that teaches the experiment to a non-specialist first and preserves the complete technical audit underneath.

## Scope
Rename the navigation label while retaining the stable route; add a simple project introduction; render the frozen chronological experiment as a five-step visual/text sequence; introduce metrics only after the question; connect every public number to the explanation catalog; show data provenance, supported/unsupported claims, team-context confound, external replication, null result, uncertainty and engineering/AI boundaries; retain direct evidence and artifact links; provide mobile and no-JavaScript reading orders.

## Non-goals
No new result, data recomputation, route removal, marketing superlative, separate About page, reduction of the advanced audit, client-only critical content, identity-challenge implementation or visual rebrand outside the approved frontend primitives.

## Stop condition
If the route cannot render a required value or explainer from versioned evidence, fail closed with an evidence identifier and retain the last valid audit path; do not hard-code a replacement value or omit the affected limitation.
design: Implement against the accepted narrative specification, typed explanation catalog, shared provenance component and frontend ownership/CSS baseline. The section order is: orientation, five-step experiment, one worked example, headline versus baseline, strongest confound, uncertainty, replication/null result, supported/unsupported claims, engineering and governed-AI boundary, full provenance. Advanced experiment cards may use accessible disclosure, but supported claim, data vintage and strongest limitation remain visible by default.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Primary navigation reads `How it works`, `/science` remains the canonical static route, and all existing evidence links/fragments either remain valid or have tested compatibility anchors.
2. Above the first metric, the page answers what ScoutLens is, what question is tested, why the season is split and what a successful retrieval means using the frozen beginner-facing copy.
3. The five-step experiment has an equivalent ordered text representation and a worked profile example whose identity, periods and values resolve from the featured artifact.
4. Every metric opens or links to its typed explanation; source values exactly match artifacts after declared rounding and no component contains copied production constants.
5. Supported claim, historical-data label, team-context confound and not-recruitment boundary remain visible without expanding details at 320 px, desktop and no-JavaScript states.
6. Direct links expose controls, external replication, null result, uncertainty method, data sources, licences, artifacts and decision records without repository archaeology.
7. Unit, link, static-output, 320/360/768/1280 visual, keyboard, axe and production performance checks pass with no relaxed threshold or undocumented snapshot update.

title: Publish explicit data provenance, vintage and limitations
description:
## Outcome
Make the age, provenance, licence boundary and methodological purpose of each dataset visible before a visitor can mistake ScoutLens for a live scouting product.

## Scope
Build one artifact-backed data-vintage/provenance presentation used by landing, `/science` and `/lab`; identify Wyscout/Pappalardo and aggregate-only StatsBomb evidence; show season/competition scope, population/minutes rule, public redistribution boundary, canonical source and licence; explain why the historical snapshot is useful for a reproducible method benchmark; distinguish reproducibility from recency; provide an advanced provenance path.

## Non-goals
No new data source, current-season refresh, provider comparison claim, commercial-use interpretation beyond the recorded licence, legal advice, per-player StatsBomb exposure, duplicated manifest fields or suggestion that historical results transfer unchanged to current football.

## Stop condition
If provider season, licence or redistribution facts disagree across manifest, research summary and frozen documentation, render nothing new and open a data-contract discrepancy bead; do not choose the most convenient value in UI copy.
design: Use `manifest.json`, `research-summary.json` and their versioned source/evidence links as runtime authority. Implement a shared server-rendered provenance/vintage component plus route-specific concise variants. The first-interpretation badge says historical reproducible benchmark and names the primary season; the expanded view distinguishes primary per-profile Wyscout evidence from aggregate-only StatsBomb replication. All links remain usable without JavaScript.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Landing, `/science` and both selected and unselected `/lab` states show a visible historical-benchmark label and primary dataset season before the first result is interpreted.
2. The expanded source view identifies provider, source citation/link, licence/link, competition/season scope, eligibility threshold and public redistribution boundary directly from versioned artifacts or their stable references.
3. StatsBomb is always described as aggregate replication in the public experience; no raw or per-player StatsBomb data/link is exposed by the new UI.
4. Copy explicitly states that the project evaluates a reproducible method on historical data and does not provide current scouting information or guarantee temporal transport.
5. Tests fail if required provenance fields are absent, provider boundaries are swapped, route variants disagree, or hard-coded production season/population values appear outside the approved content boundary.
6. The concise badge and expanded disclosure are keyboard accessible, readable at 320 px and no-JavaScript safe, with no essential source hidden behind hover.
7. Unit, static-output, link, accessibility and production-build gates pass without changing source artifacts or licences.

title: Define a typed explanation catalog for public evidence
description:
## Outcome
Provide one typed, test-enforced explanation source for every metric and feature concept shown publicly, so a non-specialist can understand a number without UI components copying values or inventing scientific meaning.

## Scope
Inventory metrics rendered on landing, `/science` and `/lab`; implement explanation records keyed by stable metric, feature, caveat and evidence identifiers; define plain meaning, calculation summary, scale/direction, interpretation boundary and source link; reuse existing artifact labels, descriptions and units; expose accessible inline and expanded variants; add completeness and orphan detection tests.

## Non-goals
No result value, interval, rank, population size or season constant in the explanation registry; no scientific formula change; no new artifact schema unless a separately reviewed contract gap blocks implementation; no visual page redesign; no LLM-authored runtime explanations.

## Stop condition
If an explanation requires a fact not represented by a versioned artifact or frozen method document, fail the completeness review and create a contract/content dependency rather than embedding the fact ad hoc in a component.
design: Create `web/src/content/evidence-explanations.ts` as the presentation-owned, non-numeric registry and `web/tests/evidence-explanations.test.ts` as its contract test. Values, labels, units, intervals and populations continue to come from generated showcase types and loaded artifacts. Explanations reference stable IDs and repository evidence links. Components consume the registry through one resolver that throws a typed incompatible-content error on unknown required IDs; they do not carry local tooltip prose.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The registry defines `plainMeaning`, `calculationSummary`, `scaleAndDirection`, `notMeaning`, and `evidenceHref` for every public headline/retrieval metric; optional `example` text contains no copied production value.
2. Every one of the 32 feature definitions resolves to its artifact-owned label, description and unit plus a plain-language interpretation boundary; no higher-is-better implication is introduced.
3. Caveat and evidence identifiers resolve through stable keys, and the resolver fails closed for an unknown required key instead of returning generic prose.
4. Tests enumerate the production research and featured-profile fixtures and fail for missing explainers, orphan explainers, duplicate keys, forbidden recommendation/quality/currentness language and numeric result literals.
5. Inline summaries and expanded explanations expose identical semantics to visual, keyboard and screen-reader users; tooltip-only access is prohibited.
6. `rg`/AST assertions demonstrate that rendered metric values still originate in artifacts and that page/component files do not introduce duplicate headline constants.
7. `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and the generated-contract check pass with no showcase schema or generated file diff.

title: Freeze beginner-facing narrative and information architecture
description:
## Outcome
Freeze an implementation-ready beginner-facing narrative and information architecture before any page or visual redesign, so every later writer or frontend agent communicates the same experiment and claim boundary.

## Scope
Define primary and secondary audiences; the six questions a first-time reader must answer; one-sentence and 30-second explanations; vocabulary progression; route-by-route message hierarchy; progressive-disclosure layers; CTA order; placement of dataset vintage, uncertainty, limitations, engineering and governed-AI content; mobile reading order; and the relationship between landing, `/science`, `/lab` and the release case study.

## Non-goals
No React/CSS implementation, visual styling, new metric, data refresh, experiment redesign, copied numeric result, formal scout study, localization, or change to the frozen supported/unsupported claims.

## Rationale
The current public experience contains strong evidence but assumes technical context too early. Freezing the explanatory sequence first prevents a visual redesign from becoming a second, inconsistent scientific narrative and gives delegated agents a bounded content contract.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Add a separate `/about` page: rejected because it would duplicate `/science`, split provenance links and create two competing explanations.
2. Keep `/science` expert-only and simplify only the landing: rejected because metric definitions, sources and limitations still need a durable public home.
3. Let the implementing frontend agent invent copy in place: rejected because it mixes product, scientific and visual authority and is not reviewable as one decision.

## Deliverables
Create `docs/public-experience-narrative.md` as the normative product-content specification and add one decision-log entry that records the chosen public thesis, the retained `/science` URL with `How it works` navigation label, rejected alternatives and change-control boundary.

## Stop condition
If a plain-language formulation changes the scientific claim, omits the team-context confound, implies current scouting or cannot be supported by an existing evidence ID, stop and request scientific review; do not solve the conflict with softer or more promotional wording.
design: This is a product decision task owned by documentation only: `docs/public-experience-narrative.md`, the existing flagship specification and the decision log. It may quote artifact identifiers but must not add result values as a second source of truth. The specification must define exact section order separately for desktop and narrow screens, plus which material is initially visible, expandable or linked to the advanced audit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `docs/public-experience-narrative.md` names a curious non-specialist as the entry audience and technical hiring managers, engineers and data scientists as deeper-audit audiences, with explicit jobs-to-be-done for each.
2. The spec freezes one plain-language thesis, one 30-second explanation and six timed comprehension questions with canonical answers and evidence links.
3. A glossary progression defines when and how to introduce fingerprint, chronological split, candidate pool, rank, reciprocal rank/MRR, percentile, statistical neighbor, confound and match-resampled uncertainty; each term includes forbidden shorthand.
4. A route matrix assigns every required message and CTA to landing, `/science`, `/lab` or `docs/case-study.md`, identifies the single owner, and forbids duplicated metric constants.
5. Desktop and <=360 px content-order wireflows specify progressive-disclosure states and keep the supported claim, data vintage and strongest limitation visible without expansion.
6. The claims/copy matrix includes historical benchmark framing, provider/licence boundaries, AI allowlist and prohibited recommendation, quality, style-proof, currentness and future-prediction implications.
7. A decision-log entry records the selected architecture, rejected separate-About-page and science-only alternatives, review boundary and required dependencies for implementation.

title: Harden and delegate the frontend experience safely
description:
## Outcome
Create a resilient, accessible and explicitly delegable frontend workstream that fixes current responsive defects, supports the new flagship narrative and identity interaction, and prevents visual regressions without granting a frontend agent authority over scientific semantics or data contracts.

## Scope
Audit every public route across a frozen viewport and content matrix; define allowed and forbidden file ownership for a specialist frontend agent; reduce the collision risk of the monolithic stylesheet; repair shared shell, landing and science defects; harden the complete Lab hierarchy under long content and uncertainty; expand visual, overflow, overlap, zoom, keyboard, accessibility and performance release gates; integrate the existing JavaScript-headroom bead instead of duplicating it.

## Non-goals
No scientific metric, claim, caveat or algorithm change; no edits to provider data, research artifacts, schemas or generated contracts; no framework migration, backend, authentication, design-system rewrite for its own sake, unreviewed rebrand, arbitrary snapshot regeneration, relaxed performance/accessibility thresholds, or product feature not owned by a separate product bead.

## Success boundary
The epic closes only when an independent frontend agent can select one ready child, know exactly which files and semantics it may touch, reproduce the defect, implement within one bounded PR, and provide objective before/after and automated evidence without requiring unstated design judgment.
design:
The default delegated allowlist is `web/src/app/**`, presentation-only components under `web/src/components/**`, route-scoped styles and `web/e2e/**`. `web/src/content/**` may be changed only when a child explicitly names the file and prohibits value/claim changes. The denylist is `src/scoutlens/**`, `config/**`, `schemas/**`, `web/src/contracts/generated/**`, `public/showcase/**`, `artifacts/**`, frozen research reports and any command that regenerates scientific outputs. Crossing the boundary stops the task and creates a dependency or review request; it is never bundled into a frontend PR.

Delivery protocol: one bead, one branch and one narrowly scoped PR; no two agents edit the same route stylesheet concurrently; each PR records viewport-specific before/after screenshots, DOM/accessibility evidence, exact quality commands and bundle measurements. Snapshot updates require an enumerated intended-difference list. CSS modularization must preserve rendered output before visual fixes begin.

Execution boundary: this epic is a non-executable container. Never claim it; claim only a ready leaf. Planned order: scoutlens-uze.1 -> uze.2 -> uze.3 -> uze.4; uze.5 waits for uncertainty and identity surfaces; uze.6 is the final release gate.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every direct child is closed with evidence, the final responsive quality gate passes, and the existing `scoutlens-jtt.14` JavaScript-headroom target is met without relaxed budgets.
2. At 320, 360, 375, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 CSS pixels, landing, `/science` and selected/unselected `/lab` states have no page-level horizontal scroll, clipped essential content, unintended overlap, off-screen controls or inaccessible internal scroll regions under normal and maximum-content fixtures.
3. At 200% browser zoom and with long player/team/competition names, all essential content reflows, keyboard focus remains visible, touch targets remain at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels and no analytical meaning depends on hover, color or animation.
4. Automated screenshots cover all three routes and critical Lab states on mobile and desktop; geometry assertions cover known overlap risks; overflow assertions run per route; axe reports no serious or critical violations.
5. The stylesheet ownership/layering decision is implemented sufficiently that separate route work does not require concurrent edits to one monolithic selector block; the migration produces no undocumented visual change.
6. Git diff and tests prove no delegated frontend delivery changes scientific artifacts, schema/generated contracts, metric values, evidence IDs, claim boundaries or provider licences.
7. The agent handoff template names allowed files, forbidden files, reproduction steps, acceptance commands, required screenshots, stop conditions and escalation path; at least one child is demonstrably executable from that contract without extra interpretation.

title: Make the flagship understandable and unmistakably differentiated
description:
## Outcome
Make ScoutLens understandable to a curious non-specialist within 90 seconds while preserving the exact scientific claim boundaries, and make the public experience unmistakably about temporal player identity evidence rather than a generic football dashboard.

## Scope
Define the beginner-facing audience and story; progressively disclose the experiment, metrics, datasets, uncertainty, limitations, engineering and governed-AI role; keep `/science` as the canonical route while allowing a clearer navigation label; add a deterministic identity-challenge interaction; make source, season, licence and historical-benchmark framing visible; provide a shared explanation model for public metrics and features; validate comprehension and claim consistency before the portfolio case study.

## Non-goals
No current-player scouting product, recommendation workflow, quality or style ranking, new provider or season ingestion, recruitment validation, marketing claim beyond the frozen claims matrix, duplicated numeric constants in UI copy, LLM-generated scientific truth, multilingual release requirement, or replacement of the advanced audit trail.

## Success boundary
The epic is not complete because pages exist. It closes only after a first-time-reader checklist can recover the question, method, supported result, largest limitation, data vintage and AI role from the public experience without repository archaeology, and all values still resolve from versioned evidence artifacts.
design:
Preserve `/science` for stable evidence links but present it in the navigation as `How it works`. Use three layers: (1) plain-language orientation, (2) guided experiment and result explanation, and (3) advanced scientific/provenance audit. Artifact-owned values remain authoritative; the explanatory content layer may define wording keyed by stable metric, feature, caveat and evidence IDs but must never own copied result values. Historical data is labeled as a reproducible benchmark, never disguised as a live dataset. The identity challenge renders only deterministic stored outputs and reveals the experiment rather than gamifying player quality.

Ownership boundary: scientific meaning and values remain owned by `src/scoutlens/**`, `config/**`, `schemas/**`, generated contracts, `public/showcase/**` and frozen research documents. Narrative work may propose a cross-boundary change only through a separate reviewed bead; it may not silently change any of those surfaces while implementing presentation.

Execution boundary: this epic is a non-executable container. Never claim it; claim only a ready leaf. Planned order: scoutlens-9a3.1; then 9a3.2, 9a3.3 and 9a3.5; then 9a3.4 and 9a3.6 when their frontend/science blockers close; finish with 9a3.7.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every direct child is closed with Definition-of-Done evidence and the final integration gate is green.
2. Landing, `/science` and the guided Lab entry use one tested plain-language thesis and one claims matrix; no route implies recommendation, player quality, style proof, current scouting or future prediction.
3. A timed external-reader checklist is executable against the built site and demonstrates that a new reader can answer six fixed questions within 90 seconds: what was tested, how the chronological comparison works, what the headline result means, what it does not mean, which historical datasets were used, and what AI is allowed to do.
4. Every public headline and retrieval metric has a stable explainer covering meaning, computation summary, scale/direction, misuse boundary and evidence/source link; tests fail on missing or orphaned mappings and numeric values are never duplicated outside artifacts.
5. Dataset provider, competition/season vintage, population threshold, licence boundary and historical-benchmark purpose are visible at the point of first interpretation and in the provenance audit.
6. The public experience includes one deterministic identity-challenge flow with keyboard, touch, no-JavaScript/degraded and direct-link behavior; its reveal exactly matches stored artifacts and includes the strongest applicable caveat and uncertainty state.
7. Production build, unit, E2E, accessibility, visual, static-integrity and performance gates pass without relaxed budgets, and `docs/case-study.md` can consume the same narrative without becoming a second source of metrics.

title: Decide bootstrap memory remediation after 4 GiB breach
description: Outcome: choose and document the smallest engineering change that brings match_bootstrap_v1 below the frozen 4 GiB peak-RSS target without changing draws, estimands, numeric rules, outputs or validity. Evidence on the documented Windows machine: workers=2 completed 500/500 in 52.06 s at 4,991,041,536 bytes peak RSS; workers=1 completed 500/500 in 63.52 s at 4,991,221,760 bytes; both wrote 288,373,735 checkpoint bytes and 1,664,262 final Parquet bytes. The worker-invariant peak points to allocator retention or summarization. Scope: phase-isolated measurement and architecture decision only; non-goals: relaxing 4 GiB, reducing 500 draws, changing cohort/features/ranks, or suppressing provenance.
design: Run clean subprocess measurements for preparation/replicates and summary-only against the completed compatible checkpoints. If process isolation alone keeps each phase below 4 GiB, choose a staged CLI that releases the replicate process before summary; otherwise choose a bounded-memory summary that scans/project columns instead of retaining the complete wide frame. Verify candidate output Parquet bytes/hashes against the completed workers=1 and workers=2 references. Record rationale and rejected alternative in the decisions log, then define the implementation follow-up with exact verification commands.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Peak RSS and elapsed time are recorded separately for replicate and summary phases on the same machine and 500-resample checkpoints. 2. One remediation is selected with evidence that its projected/measured peak is <=4 GiB; if neither candidate works, the decision explicitly blocks publication. 3. The decision preserves match_bootstrap_v1 and requires byte-identical feature, retrieval and neighbor Parquets versus both completed reference runs. 4. A decisions-log entry records evidence, tradeoffs, chosen boundary and rollback/failure behavior. 5. A narrowly specified implementation bead is created and linked as blocking scoutlens-jtt.5.2.
notes: Decision recorded as D032. Eager workers=2: 52.06 s/4,991,041,536 B; eager workers=1: 63.52 s/4,991,221,760 B; streaming workers=2: 50.44 s/1,127,751,680 B. Chosen projected lazy/streaming aggregation; rejected one-worker and process isolation. All three final Parquet hashes identical across references.
