title: Serve the built 404 page for unknown routes in the release fixture
description:
## Outcome

An unknown route on the production static fixture returns an unstyled plain-text dead end. The built 404 page exists and is never served, so it is also never exercised by any release gate.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. cd web && pnpm build
2. node scripts/serve-static.mjs --port 4173
3. curl -i http://127.0.0.1:4173/definitely-missing/

## Expected

The contents of web/out/404.html with HTTP status 404: site header, primary navigation, site footer and an h1 of '404'. Requesting http://127.0.0.1:4173/404.html directly today returns exactly that page with status 200, so the asset is correct and only the routing is missing.

## Observed

HTTP/1.1 404 with Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 and body 'Not found'. The rendered document contains zero .site-header, zero .site-footer and zero focusable elements, measured 2026-08-04 at 360, 320 and 1280 CSS pixels. A visitor who mistypes a URL or follows a stale link has no navigation back.

## Root cause

web/scripts/serve-static.mjs:75 returns the literal string for any pathname that fileFor() cannot resolve, instead of falling back to out/404.html.

## Why it matters beyond the fixture

scripts/serve-static.mjs is what pnpm release:check serves to Playwright and Lighthouse. Because it never serves 404.html, the built 404 page has no coverage at all, and the fixture does not represent how a static host resolves a missing path.

## Non-goals

No change to the 404 page design or copy, no rewrite/redirect rules beyond the missing-path fallback, no change to the cache-control policy for existing paths, no framework or hosting change.

## Evidence

docs/frontend-qa-audit.md section F-2; web/test-results/frontend-qa-audit/probe.json#notFound and #notFoundAsset.
design:
Only the unresolved-path branch changes: read out/404.html, respond 404 with text/html and the existing security headers, and keep the current no-cache policy for HTML. Preserve the existing 405 handling for non-GET/HEAD and the existing directory-traversal guard. If out/404.html is absent, keep the current plain-text body rather than failing to start.

Ownership note: web/scripts/** is outside the default delegated frontend allowlist in scoutlens-uze. Confirm ownership before starting.
acceptance_criteria:
1. GET /definitely-missing/ returns status 404, Content-Type text/html; charset=utf-8, and a body containing .site-header, .site-footer and an h1 of '404'.
2. HEAD on the same path returns 404 with no body.
3. Existing 200 responses, gzip negotiation, Cache-Control values, Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options and the traversal guard are unchanged; the existing quality-contract cache-header test still passes.
4. A regression test in web/e2e asserts the 404 status, content type, presence of primary navigation and at least one focusable element.
5. The 404 response has no page-level horizontal overflow and no serious or critical axe violation at 320 and 1280 CSS pixels.
6. pnpm release:check passes.

title: Provide deterministic maximum-content and uncertainty-state Lab fixtures
description:
## Outcome

Two cells of the scoutlens-uze.1 responsive matrix could not be exercised against published data. Provide deterministic fixtures so both become auditable and gate-able without editing production showcase artifacts.

## Blocked cell 1 — selector list under maximum identity content

web/src/app/lab/page.tsx consumes players.index.json in a server component, so the 1,257-row result list is baked into the static export. Playwright HTTP interception can only replace the lazily fetched players/<key>.json, never the rendered list. Stretching the list today would require editing public/showcase/v1/players.index.json, which is a denied artifact.

Longest values actually present in the published catalog (measured 2026-08-04):
- display_name: 'K. Théophile Catherine' (22 chars, wy-25643-c-412)
- team join: 'Saint-Étienne / Olympique Marseille' (35 chars, wy-25999-c-412)
- most teams in one period: 2
- competition name: 'Spanish first division' (22 chars)

## Blocked cell 2 — uncertainty available/insufficient

All 1,257 published profiles carry uncertainty_status: 'pending'. The 'available' and 'insufficient' branches of rankStabilityText() and stabilityText() were audited only through an HTTP fixture with a recomputed manifest sha256. That is valid layout evidence but is not published data, so no gate can assert it.

## Scope

Add a build- or test-time fixture mechanism that can render both the selector list and a selected profile under maximum identity content, and can render each uncertainty status, using data that is deterministic and version-controlled outside the published showcase pack.

## Non-goals

No edit to public/showcase/v1/**, no change to any metric, rank, neighbor or uncertainty value, no dev-only data path reachable from the production export, no schema change.
design:
Prefer a fixture pack that the existing Playwright suite can point the static export at, or a test-only build variant, over any runtime switch shipped to production. Any synthetic identity must stay obviously synthetic and must never appear in a released build. The manifest-checksum recomputation used by e2e/failure-states.spec.ts is the established precedent for profile-level fixtures; the gap is list-level and build-time.

Recorded harness reference: web/test-results/frontend-qa-audit/audit.mjs (installProfileFixture, stretchIdentity, resolveUncertainty) demonstrates the profile-level technique that already works.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The Lab selector list can be rendered with at least one profile whose display name, team join and competition name each exceed the published maximum by a stated margin, without modifying any file under public/showcase/v1/.
2. A profile can be rendered with retrieval uncertainty status 'available' (with rank_ci_95, median_rank, valid_resamples and all three recall rates populated) and with status 'insufficient', both passing the existing schema and checksum validation.
3. Neighbor stability 'available' and 'insufficient' render through the same mechanism.
4. The fixtures are deterministic: two runs produce identical DOM for the same fixture id.
5. scoutlens-uze.6 can assert responsive geometry against these fixtures at 320, 360, 768 and 1280 CSS pixels.
6. The production export built by pnpm build contains no fixture identity and no fixture code path; a check proves it.
7. docs/frontend-qa-audit.md blocked-cell rows are updated to reference the delivered fixture ids.

title: Make Windows RSS probe type-check on Linux CI
description:
## Outcome
Keep the native Windows peak-RSS measurement while making scoutlens.uncertainty.run pass Mypy on Linux/Python 3.14.

## Steps to Reproduce
On the PR merge ref under Ubuntu/Python 3.14, run uv run --frozen mypy src/scoutlens. Typeshed reports attr-defined for ctypes.WinDLL, ctypes.WinError and ctypes.get_last_error in uncertainty/run.py. Windows Mypy passes because those symbols exist in the platform-specific ctypes interface.

## Root Cause
Linux typeshed intentionally omits Windows-only ctypes attributes even though the code branch is runtime-guarded by os.name.

## Scope
Access only the Windows loader/error surface through an Any-typed facade, validate both Mypy platforms and regenerate production provenance. Non-goals: disabling Mypy rules or changing bootstrap computations.
design: Access only the platform-specific ctypes loader/error surface through an Any-typed Windows facade; retain typed portable ctypes structures and calls. Regenerate the production run because source_sha256 changes, then verify final Parquet hashes remain identical.
acceptance_criteria: 1. mypy src/scoutlens passes on Windows and mypy --platform linux src/scoutlens passes locally. 2. Native peak_resident_memory_bytes returns a positive value on Windows. 3. Full 500-resample run remains below targets and the three Parquet SHA-256 values are unchanged. 4. GitHub static-quality passes.
notes: Fixed in 5a6bcdd using an Any-typed facade only for Windows-exclusive ctypes APIs. Local Mypy passes on Windows and --platform linux; native probe returns positive RSS. Final-source production run: 500/500, 50.83 s, 1,134,657,536 B peak; all three Parquet hashes unchanged. GitHub Actions run 30501895285: static-quality, pytest 3.11, pytest 3.14 and web-quality all pass.

title: Normalize literal Unicode escapes in showcase identity fields
description:
## Outcome

Eliminate literal Unicode escape sequences from user-visible player, team and competition identity fields at the showcase producer boundary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate showcase v1 from the current Wyscout inputs.
2. Parse players.index.json or a player profile as JSON.
3. Inspect display_name or team name values for accented identities such as A. Begovic or Atletico Madrid.
4. Observe that the parsed string still contains literal \u0107 or \u00e9 text instead of the Unicode character.

## Observed Behavior

Escaped text is widespread across the index and profiles. The evidence story currently applies a narrow display-name workaround only to protect the featured release.

## Expected Behavior

Canonical JSON contains real UTF-8 identity text after parsing, with consistent values in index and profiles and valid manifest digests.

## Scope

Normalize trusted identity strings once before artifact construction; do not add independent UI decoders.
design: Normalize trusted identity strings once before artifact construction, not independently in each UI. Decode only valid Unicode escape sequences, preserve ordinary backslashes and malformed text, then regenerate canonical UTF-8 artifacts and manifest hashes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. After JSON parsing, players.index.json and every player profile contain no literal valid Unicode escape sequence in display_name, team name or competition identity fields. 2. Tests cover single and multiple escapes, accented player/team names, ordinary backslashes and malformed escape text. 3. Index/profile identity values remain consistent and the showcase validator plus manifest digest checks pass. 4. Showcase v1 artifacts are regenerated with correct UTF-8 names. 5. The web-only decode workaround is removed and its story tests still pass.

title: Enforce exact cardinality for v1 confidence intervals
description:
## Outcome
Make every v1 confidence-interval array accept exactly two numeric bounds under JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and compile under Ajv strict tuple validation.

## Scope
The five prefixItems branches in src/scoutlens/showcase/schemas/showcase-1.0.0.schema.json, Python schema tests, regenerated TypeScript/schema outputs, public manifest provenance, and the web Ajv configuration.

## Steps to Reproduce
From web, run pnpm test with new Ajv2020({ allErrors: true, strict: true }); importing the generated v1 schema. Ajv throws strict mode prefixItems is 2-tuple but minItems or maxItems are not specified at feature_uncertainty.raw_ci_95 before any repository test runs. The same omission exists at five schema locations found with rg prefixItems.

## Non-goals
Do not change interval estimation, uncertainty semantics, UI rendering, dataset values, or add interval fields.

## Dependency
Execute after scoutlens-jtt.4.2.

## Release rule
Treat this as a pre-v1 validation correction and retain schema_version 1.0.0 only if docs/decisions-log.md records why the stricter schema does not change valid artifact shape. Otherwise create a versioned migration bead before implementation.
design: Add minItems: 2 and maxItems: 2 beside items: false in raw_ci_95, within_role_percentile_ci_95, rank_uncertainty.rank_ci_95, neighbor_stability.rank_ci_95, and research_metric.ci_95. Add parameterized schema tests for null, valid two-item arrays, and invalid lengths 0, 1, and 3 for all five locations. Regenerate web/src/contracts/generated/showcase.ts and showcase.schema.json from the Python-owned schema, remove strictTuples: false from StaticShowcaseRepository, rebuild the public manifest through the exporter, and record the pre-release contract correction in the decision log.
acceptance_criteria: 1. All five interval array branches declare minItems=2 and maxItems=2 while retaining items=false. 2. Parameterized Python tests prove null and length 2 are accepted and lengths 0, 1, and 3 are rejected for every interval field. 3. web/src/contracts/showcase-repository.ts compiles Ajv with strict tuple validation enabled and its repository tests pass. 4. uv run --frozen pytest tests/showcase -q, web pnpm contracts:check, lint, typecheck, test, and build all exit 0. 5. The regenerated public manifest records the new schema input digest and validates through validate_published_directory. 6. docs/decisions-log.md states the compatibility rationale and confirms no valid published artifact shape or numerical result changed.
notes: Implemented exact minItems/maxItems cardinality across all five v1 confidence intervals; added 25 invalid-cardinality and 10 valid/null parameter cases; restored strict Ajv compilation; normalized draft-2020 tuples only for json-schema-to-typescript compiler input so generated types are [number, number]; regenerated schema/types/public manifest; documented D029 compatibility rationale. Validation: showcase 33 passed/1 skipped; full Python 216 passed/6 skipped; Ruff, mypy, uv build; web contracts/check, lint, typecheck, 5 tests, Next build/static check; validate_published_directory passed. Manifest comparison confirms all 1,260 file entries, population, source and non-schema inputs unchanged; only schema provenance and producer identity changed.
close_reason: All six acceptance criteria verified; no numerical result or valid published artifact shape changed.

title: Freeze and audit the v1 release candidate
description: Outcome: produce one immutable v1 release candidate whose scientific claims, artifacts, dependencies, licences, security posture and build inputs are known before deployment. Scope: version/schema/dataset freeze, claims matrix, clean-tree gates, dependency and secret audit, third-party licences/attribution, browser privacy review and SBOM/inventory. title: Integrate optional AI explanation with deterministic fallback
description: Outcome: add a clearly optional explanation action to the comparison experience while preserving the complete deterministic evidence UI. Scope: consentful trigger, loading, validated result with evidence links, unavailable/invalid/timeout fallback, cache status, non-AI disclosure and accessibility. Non-goals: replacing contribution tables, automatic calls on page load, general chat, saved conversation or advice.
design: Do not call a model until the user requests an explanation. Render validated structured sections and link each statement to existing evidence rows. On any failure, show a concise reason category and the deterministic evidence, never raw provider output. The application build and all non-online tests work with AI disabled.
acceptance_criteria: 1) no model request occurs on route load or profile selection; 2) successful output displays provider/model disclosure and every cited evidence ID resolves to visible evidence; 3) disabled, credential-missing, timeout, rate-limit, invalid-output and offline fixtures preserve the full deterministic flow; 4) raw invalid output and secrets never reach browser/logs; 5) keyboard, screen-reader, mobile and reduced-motion checks pass; 6) performance budget excludes lazy AI code until triggered and remains within limits; 7) E2E proves the app is fully useful with AI disabled; 8) local eval thresholds are green.

title: Build local grounded-explanation eval suite
description: Outcome: quantify whether the explanation layer stays factual and appropriately limited across representative, adversarial and degraded evidence. Scope: versioned evaluation corpus, deterministic validators, offline replay, optional live-provider runner, metrics, thresholds, failure reports and regression snapshots. Non-goals: subjective football correctness judged without evidence or dependence on a hosted eval service.
design: Create at least 60 cases spanning roles, strong/weak alignments, null/imputed features, available/insufficient uncertainty, small samples, forbidden recruitment prompts, injection attempts, missing evidence and provider errors. Metrics: schema validity, evidence citation coverage, exact numeric support, critical caveat retention, forbidden-claim/refusal success and fallback correctness. Separate deterministic gate from informative model-quality rubric.
acceptance_criteria: 1) corpus has at least 60 uniquely identified cases and coverage matrix; 2) deterministic gate requires 100 percent supported entities/numbers, 100 percent critical caveat retention, 100 percent forbidden-claim rejection and 100 percent correct degraded fallback; 3) happy-path live structured validity target is at least 95 percent over three fixed-seed runs where the provider supports seeding, otherwise three recorded runs; 4) failures produce minimal evidence/output/validator diagnostics without secrets; 5) offline replay is deterministic and required in CI; 6) optional live runner records provider/model/prompt/schema versions, tokens, latency and cost; 7) threshold misses block integration or produce an explicit DROP decision.

title: Implement swappable structured explanation provider
description: Outcome: implement one production structured-output model adapter behind a provider-neutral interface plus deterministic offline stubs. Scope: request construction from evidence bundles, schema-constrained response, prompt/version metadata, timeout, one bounded retry for transport failure, evidence-hash cache, token/latency/cost telemetry and validated fallback. Non-goals: agent loops, web browsing, RAG, tool calls, conversation memory or exposing credentials to the browser.
design: The server/build-side provider accepts one immutable evidence bundle and returns untrusted structured output that must pass jtt.6.1 validation. Use environment credentials only in explicit online mode. Cache key includes model/provider, prompt/schema versions and evidence hash. Timeout target is 8 seconds; no retry on validation failure; never log secrets or free-form player search text.
acceptance_criteria: 1) interface, offline fake and production adapter share contract tests; 2) valid structured response passes validator and invalid/timeout/rate-limit/auth/network responses yield typed fallback; 3) at most one transport retry and no validation retry are proven in tests; 4) cache invalidates on evidence/prompt/schema/model change; 5) browser bundle contains no secret or provider SDK; 6) per-call model/version, input/output token counts, latency and estimated cost are observable without personal data; 7) online smoke test is opt-in while offline CI remains complete; 8) dependency, lint, type and security checks pass.

title: Define AI evidence bundle and fail-closed validator
description: Outcome: create the provider-independent contract that strictly bounds what an explanation may say. Scope: evidence-bundle schema, output schema, allow-listed entities/features/evidence IDs, numeric formatting rules, mandatory caveat policy, forbidden-intent policy, deterministic validator, adversarial fixtures and versioned prompt contract. Non-goals: model calls, UI, free-form chat or semantic retrieval.
design: Build evidence bundles only from validated showcase profile data. Require every factual sentence/section to cite evidence IDs. Structured output separates summary, alignments, disagreements, uncertainty and caveats. Validator rejects unknown IDs/entities, numbers outside declared formatted evidence, missing critical caveats, recommendation/quality/future claims and outputs exceeding length. No repair-by-invention; invalid output falls back.
acceptance_criteria: 1) versioned input/output JSON Schemas and typed Python/TypeScript representations exist; 2) bundle builder is deterministic and contains only selected profile/neighbor evidence plus mandatory caveats; 3) validator accepts canonical valid fixtures and rejects 100 percent of fixtures for fabricated entity, feature, value, citation, omitted caveat, recommendation, style proof and prompt-injection content; 4) number-format equivalence rules have boundary tests; 5) schemas/prompts have explicit versions and evidence hash; 6) default CI runs without network/model credentials; 7) trust-boundary documentation and threat table are complete.

title: Evaluate cross-provider behavior and decide KEEP or DROP
description: Outcome: make the final complexity decision using the frozen Wyscout test and untouched StatsBomb canonical replication, including scientific and operational costs. Scope: apply Wyscout-trained canonical-28 transformations without StatsBomb tuning, paired uncertainty, provider/role failure analysis, threshold table, D-log decision and artifact disposition. Non-goals: salvaging a miss with new tuning or recruitment claims.
design: Evaluate cosine, diagonal and any gated neural representation on identical StatsBomb canonical queries after all Wyscout choices are frozen. Apply every preregistered KEEP clause conjunctively. KEEP promotes one representation with versioned artifacts and public caveats; DROP preserves code/results as a documented null and leaves cosine authoritative.

title: Run conditional neural contrastive benchmark
description: Outcome: either document a preregistered no-go without training or benchmark one compact neural contrastive representation after the diagonal model passes its continuation gate. Scope: one frozen architecture family, validation-only early stopping, deterministic training, same splits/pairs/metrics, ablation versus diagonal metric, calibration and operational cost. Non-goals: architecture search, foundation models, provider-specific tuning or treating a skipped run as missing work.
design: First read the recorded CONTINUE_NEURAL/STOP_NEURAL decision. On STOP, close with protocol evidence and no model. On CONTINUE, use one small MLP projection with fixed depth/width range declared before training, contrastive loss over the same positives/hard negatives, early stopping on validation MRR and one final test evaluation. Export weights only for evaluation, not automatic product adoption.
acceptance_criteria: 1) gate evidence is machine-readable and matches qop.2; 2) STOP path performs no training and records why complexity was not earned; 3) CONTINUE path has fixed seeds, architecture/search limits, checkpoint provenance and reproducible learning curves; 4) neural, diagonal and cosine share exact test queries and candidate pools; 5) paired metrics, calibration, failure cases and role subgroups are reported; 6) training/inference time, peak memory and artifact size are recorded; 7) no test-result-driven retraining occurs.

title: Benchmark interpretable diagonal metric
description: Outcome: measure the simplest trainable alternative to cosine: non-negative per-feature weights learned from temporal pairs. Scope: training objective, regularization, validation-only hyperparameter selection, same-role hard negatives, calibrated retrieval outputs, paired uncertainty, role analysis, learned-weight interpretation and runtime/artifact cost. Non-goals: neural embeddings, test-driven tuning or replacing the public baseline before the final gate.
design: Implement a diagonal metric over frozen standardized features so the result stays auditable. Positives are same-player A/B pairs; negatives are distinct same-role players sampled deterministically. Constrain weights non-negative, normalize scale, tune a small preregistered regularization grid on validation, then evaluate the selected model once on Wyscout test. Compare to cosine on identical queries/candidates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) training and inference are deterministic for the frozen seed; 2) leakage, negative-sampling, serialization and zero/degenerate-weight tests pass; 3) all preregistered validation choices and the one-time test result are saved with manifests; 4) paired delta intervals and every declared subgroup are reported; 5) weight table identifies unstable or collapsed families without quality-language overreach; 6) training time, inference time, artifact bytes and maintenance delta are recorded; 7) an explicit CONTINUE_NEURAL or STOP_NEURAL decision applies the preregistered validation gate without exception.

title: Preregister player-disjoint representation benchmark
description: Outcome: freeze the confirmatory benchmark before any learned model is fitted. Scope: immutable Wyscout player-disjoint train/validation/test split, canonical StatsBomb external test, populations, preprocessing, negative sampling, baseline, metrics, paired intervals, subgroup rules, practical-gain threshold, neural continuation gate and compute budgets. Non-goals: looking at test labels while designing, UMAP evidence or recruitment endpoints.
design: Use deterministic role-stratified 60/20/20 Wyscout player splits; every competition-period row for one human stays in one split. Fit preprocessing and models on train only; select on validation; open test once. Primary metric is within-role temporal-retrieval MRR; secondary global MRR, median rank and Recall@1/5/10. Canonical 28-feature Wyscout training produces frozen weights for provider-native StatsBomb evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) versioned benchmark protocol and split manifest with seed/hash/counts exist; 2) tests prove zero player overlap and no fitted statistic reads validation/test; 3) frozen baselines reproduce on all splits; 4) KEEP threshold is Wyscout test delta MRR at least +0.020 with paired 95 percent CI lower above 0, no role subgroup with at least 100 queries drops more than 0.020, StatsBomb delta is positive with lower bound above -0.010, and operational budgets pass; 5) neural continuation requires diagonal-model validation delta at least +0.010 with CI lower above -0.005; 6) test set remains unopened until protocol hash is recorded in D-log.

title: Render honest uncertainty in the Lab
description: Outcome: visualize sampling stability without implying causal confidence or hiding unstable cases. Scope: per-feature intervals, identity-rank range and recall stability, neighbor top-five/rank stability, available/insufficient/pending states, method disclosure and accessible textual equivalents. Non-goals: player risk score, one composite confidence grade, animation-dependent meaning or AI interpretation.
design: Add intervals to the existing fingerprint and evidence components, not a parallel dashboard. Use position/shape plus text, never color alone. Keep point estimate visible; label intervals match-resampled sampling stability. Insufficient renders valid count and explanation. Method disclosure links to uncertainty-method and states excluded uncertainty sources.
acceptance_criteria: 1) available, insufficient and pending fixtures render distinct tested copy and geometry; 2) every interval/rate equals the profile artifact after display rounding; 3) inverted/invalid intervals fail at the repository boundary; 4) keyboard and screen-reader users receive point, interval, resample count and interpretation; 5) mobile layout has no overlap or hidden caveat; 6) no causal, future-performance or recruitment-confidence wording appears; 7) visual regression, accessibility, unit and E2E suites pass within existing bundle/performance budgets.

title: Implement deterministic match-bootstrap engine
description: Outcome: implement match_bootstrap_v1 as provider-scoped offline Python computation returning per-feature, all three self-rank and observed-neighbor stability distributions for the fixed Wyscout cohort. Scope: complete-match resampling, repeated-match weights, pipeline rebuild, validity accounting, SHA-256 counter-addressed parallel-safe draws and resumable intermediate output. Non-goals: UI, AI, causal intervals, alternate hierarchical models or any post-result change to the frozen estimand.
design: Implement docs/uncertainty-method.md as normative through a tested scoutlens.uncertainty module and CLI. Separate pure SHA-256 counter-addressed draw-plan generation, multiplicity-weighted replicate rebuild and type-7 summarization. Reuse canonical feature and retrieval code; keep the observed cohort fixed; rank absent candidates after present candidates; invalidate absent queries; never resample events individually or derive worker-local RNG streams. Persist gitignored Parquet checkpoints with config, source, input and draw-plan hashes plus invalid-reason totals; resume only on an exact manifest match.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The versioned synthetic fixture passes invariant, high-variance low-support, missing, tie, multi-stratum and duplicate-weight cases, including all forced draw plans. 2. Identical config/source/input produces the exact same draw-plan hash and summaries on repeated runs and with worker counts 1 and 2; reversed input order is identical. 3. Every draw preserves competition-period strata, observed stratum size, integer match multiplicity and fixed-cohort membership; absent-query, absent-candidate, zero-event and raw-null rules match docs/uncertainty-method.md. 4. Type-7 intervals, average-rank percentiles, exact ordering, numeric tolerances and the 450-of-500 availability rule match config/uncertainty.json. 5. Raw and within-role-percentile feature summaries, global/within-role/role-plus-minutes self-rank summaries and five observed-neighbor rank/top-five summaries are emitted for every fixed profile with invalid-reason counts. 6. Interrupted execution resumes only from checkpoints whose config/source/input/draw-plan manifest matches exactly; any mismatch fails closed before reuse. 7. Output provenance records both config hashes, source/input hashes, draw-plan hash, code version, requested/completed resamples and invalid-reason totals. 8. Full-data runtime, peak memory and checkpoint/final sizes are recorded; target is <=15 minutes and <=4 GiB on the documented machine. If either target or the frozen numeric contract cannot be met, stop and create a decision Bead with measurements rather than weakening the method. 9. uv run --frozen pytest -q, uv run --frozen ruff check ., uv run --frozen mypy src/scoutlens and uv build pass.
notes: Implemented deterministic match_bootstrap_v1 engine, SHA-256 draw plan, weighted sufficient-statistic rebuild, fixed-universe ranks, feature/rank/neighbor summaries, fail-closed resumable Parquet checkpoints, synthetic gate, CLI and provenance. Production: 1,257 profiles, 500/500, draw hash 05a0019e..., 50.44 s, 1.13 GB peak. Full gates and real determinism integration pass.
close_reason: Deterministic match-bootstrap engine, production run, outputs, provenance and all quality gates complete.

title: Publish uncertainty through showcase contract
description: Outcome: integrate validated match-bootstrap summaries into every relevant v1 showcase payload without breaking deterministic point-estimate consumers. Scope: available/insufficient states, feature raw and percentile intervals, self-rank stability, neighbor selection/rank stability, provenance, canonical serialization and artifact-size regression tests. Non-goals: visualization, schema-major changes or silently dropping incomplete measures.
design: Extend the exporter behind a schema-compatible minor version only if new optional fields are required; fields already specified in 1.0.0 are populated in place with a new dataset version. Join strictly on profile/period/feature/evidence identifiers and fail on duplicates or missing rows. Keep pending fixtures for degraded-state tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) every profile has one top-level uncertainty state and consistent nested states; 2) available values match engine summaries exactly and insufficient values retain valid counts with null intervals; 3) no pending remains in the production uncertainty dataset; 4) join completeness/uniqueness, bounds, rates, ranks, interval order and provenance tests pass; 5) two exports are canonically deterministic; 6) profile/catalog gzip budgets still pass or an explicit contract decision changes them; 7) the deterministic no-uncertainty fixture remains valid for web fallback tests.

title: Freeze match-bootstrap method and fixtures
description: Outcome: turn match_bootstrap_v1 from product prose into a preregistered analytical contract before implementation. Scope: estimand, strata, fixed-cohort policy, duplicate-match weighting, scaler refit, missing-replicate rules, feature/rank/neighbor outputs, seed/resamples, tolerances and synthetic truth cases. Non-goals: production optimization, web rendering or changing the fingerprint estimand after results are seen.
design: Write docs/uncertainty-method.md and add versioned uncertainty config. Use whole matches stratified by competition and period; fixed observed eligible cohort; 500 resamples seed 1729; rebuild minutes/features/combined scaler/similarity/ranks; 95 percentile intervals; insufficient below 450 valid replicates. Define behavior for zero events, absent players and tied ranks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) method document defines every sampling and missingness decision plus supported/unsupported interpretations; 2) config contains design_version, seed, resamples, interval and validity threshold; 3) synthetic fixtures include invariant players, high-variance low-support players, missing-in-resample players, tied candidates and multi-competition strata with expected qualitative outcomes; 4) unit-test tolerances and deterministic ordering are declared before production results; 5) D-log records the frozen design; 6) review checklist maps every uncertainty contract field to one computation.
notes:
Acceptance evidence (2026-07-29): AC1 docs/uncertainty-method.md freezes estimands, strata, cohort, whole-match multiplicity, scaler rebuild, missingness, validity and supported/unsupported interpretations before production execution. AC2 config/uncertainty.json v1 pins match_bootstrap_v1, seed 1729, 500 resamples, percentile_95/type-7 quantiles, 450 minimum valid observations, resampling/cohort policies, ordering, warning and tolerances. AC3 tests/uncertainty/fixtures/match_bootstrap_v1.json covers invariant, high-variance low-support, missing-in-resample, tied-candidate, multi-competition and duplicate-match cases with three forced draw plans. AC4 exact ordering and assertion tolerances are machine-pinned and CI-tested; counter-addressed SHA-256 rejection sampling includes a byte-level test vector and avoids Python-version, worker-order and modulo-bias drift. AC5 D031 records the frozen design and change control. AC6 the contract-field checklist maps all 26 top-level, feature, retrieval, neighbor and index uncertainty fields to one deterministic computation/source. The newly unblocked jtt.5.2 was refined to remove the old per-replicate-seed ambiguity, include all three retrieval outcomes, provenance and stop conditions. Validation: uncertainty contract 5 passed; full suite 229 passed and 7 skipped; Ruff clean; Mypy clean across 40 source files; sdist and wheel built. No production uncertainty result was inspected and no showcase schema or published experiment config was changed.
GitHub clean-run evidence: PR #46 workflow run 30496747764 passed pytest 3.11 in 11 s, pytest 3.14 in 12 s, static-quality in 22 s and the complete web-quality gate in 2m41. This confirms the new contract tests and documentation coexist with the clean-clone Python and web release pipeline.
close_reason: The match-bootstrap method is preregistered in normative docs, machine-pinned config and synthetic truth fixtures with drift tests, D031 and full quality gates green.

title: Ship ScoutLens v1 flagship release
description: Milestone outcome: publish a stable ScoutLens v1 portfolio release after all scientific, product and optional-technology gates have closed. Scope is production static hosting, smoke/accessibility/performance checks against the deployed URL, release documentation and media, attribution/privacy/security audit, reproducible clean-clone verification, semantic tag and rollback notes. Non-goals: adding new analytical features during release hardening.
design: Execute jtt.7.x only after jtt.4, jtt.5, jtt.6 and qop. Deployment remains static-first. README, live app and case study must use one claims matrix and one source of metrics. Release candidate freezes schema, dataset and code revisions; any analytical change returns to its owning issue.
acceptance_criteria: All jtt.7.x children closed; production URL passes smoke, WCAG and performance budgets; clean-clone build succeeds from pinned artifacts and documented commands; licences, attribution, privacy, secrets and dependency audit pass; README/case study/demo media link methods and limitations; release notes include known risks and rollback; v1 tag points to the audited commit only after CI is green.

title: Add evidence-grounded AI explanations with local evals
description: Milestone outcome: add optional natural-language explanations that can only restate deterministic profile, neighbor, contribution, uncertainty and caveat evidence. Scope is typed evidence bundles, versioned prompt/provider boundary, structured output, deterministic validation, local evals, UI fallback and observability without sensitive user data. Non-goals: computing rankings, choosing evidence, open-ended football advice, RAG, autonomous agents, or making the application depend on an LLM.

Reject unknown entities, numbers, feature claims, missing caveats and unsupported advice. Provider implementation is swappable; tests and core UI run without credentials or network.

title: Add uncertainty-aware player fingerprints
description: Milestone outcome: replace every uncertainty-pending state with interpretable match-resampled sampling stability for the public Wyscout profiles. Scope is the predeclared whole-match bootstrap, per-feature raw and percentile intervals, identity-rank stability, neighbor top-five stability, export, validation and UI. Non-goals: causal uncertainty, future prediction, provider annotation error, hierarchical modeling without a measured need, or recruitment confidence.
design: Implement child issues jtt.5.x against match_bootstrap_v1: freeze the observed eligible cohort; resample complete matches stratified by competition and period; rebuild minutes, features, scaler, similarities and ranks; 500 resamples, seed 1729, 95 percentiles, insufficient below 90 percent valid replicates. Any design change requires a decision-log entry and compatible schema version.
acceptance_criteria: All jtt.5.x children closed; synthetic tests recover stable and unstable known cases; deterministic reruns are equal within declared tolerance; every profile exports contract-valid uncertainty; UI distinguishes pending, available and insufficient without causal/recruitment language; runtime and artifact-size measurements are recorded; research and web gates pass.

title: Execute recruitment validation study
description: Optional external-study outcome: execute the already-built blinded recruitment protocol only if the project intentionally seeks a recruitment-usefulness claim and qualified raters are available. Reactivation trigger: explicit owner decision, at least two eligible independent scouts, consent/data-handling plan and frozen study materials. Non-goal: blocking or retrospectively validating the Player Fingerprint Lab flagship.
design: Keep deferred through v1. On reactivation, run the five-query discarded pilot, freeze any operational clarification before unblinding, collect approximately 600 ratings per rater, preserve arm blinding, analyze with the preregistered Wilcoxon/bootstrap/Krippendorff pipeline and publish attrition/missingness. Agent-generated or simulated ratings cannot close the issue.
acceptance_criteria: 1) reactivation trigger and rater eligibility are documented before collection; 2) at least two eligible independent scouts complete pilot and main study with deviations/attrition reported; 3) frozen shortlists remain blinded, balanced and distinct; 4) raw responses are consented, access-controlled and anonymized for analysis; 5) preregistered primary/secondary/reliability/failure metrics run without post-outcome rule changes; 6) report concludes GO, REDESIGN or NO-GO for recruitment usefulness with uncertainty/subgroups; 7) issue cannot close on harness completion, synthetic ratings or fingerprint retrieval alone.

2026-07-27 (D023): execution harness built and tested (src/scoutlens/study/) — blinded shortlist generation (40 role-stratified queries x 3 arms x 5, verified blinded/balanced/distinct on real Wyscout data) + full pre-registered analysis (Wilcoxon, bootstrap CI, Krippendorff alpha, GO/REDESIGN/NO-GO), 13 tests. STAYS OPEN: study conclusion needs real expert ratings (2-5 scouts, ~600 ratings/rater), which an agent cannot honestly provide. Remaining is data collection + running analyze_study, not a build. See docs/recruitment-study-harness.md.
Portfolio scope decision 2026-07-28: the tested flagship claim is statistical fingerprint stability, not recruitment usefulness. The completed harness remains a valid optional future study, but recruiting scouts is not required for or allowed to block the flagship.

title: Decide code license for the repository
description:
Choose the license for ScoutLens source code independently of the dataset license. This is a human publication decision and must not be inferred by an agent.

## Rationale
A public flagship release needs explicit reuse terms; no license leaves default copyright and makes reuse ambiguous.

## Alternatives Considered
- MIT: simplest permissive option.
- Apache-2.0: permissive with explicit patent terms.
- No public code license / keep private: valid if the repository is not being released for reuse.
close_reason: User decided: MIT (D019). LICENSE added, pyproject license field set, README updated, Limitation #9 closed. Code only — data licenses (CC BY 4.0 / StatsBomb constraints) unchanged.

title: Versioned run-config + data-checksum manifest, and report-vs-artifact diff test

title: Benchmark whether a learned fingerprint representation earns its place
description: Milestone outcome: decide with a preregistered, player-disjoint benchmark whether any learned fingerprint representation materially improves unseen-player temporal retrieval over frozen standardized cosine. Scope is a simple learned weighting or regularized Mahalanobis method first, a conditional neural contrastive experiment, uncertainty, calibration, compute/maintenance cost and canonical cross-provider evaluation. Non-goals: recruitment validation, exploratory UMAP as evidence, or retaining complexity after a null result.

Training positives are same-player temporal pairs and hard negatives are same-role different players. The neural stage runs only after the simple learned metric reaches its declared continuation gate; a no-go is a successful outcome when documented.

title: Apply tabular numerals to the rank figure and declare color-scheme
description:
## Outcome

Two low-severity consistency gaps found by the scoutlens-uze.1 audit, grouped because both are single-declaration changes in the same stylesheet with no layout consequence.

## Defect 1 — retrieval rank figure is not tabular

Measured 2026-08-04 on /lab/ at 1280 CSS pixels:
- .lab-fingerprint-row__values span -> font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums
- .fingerprint-value-table td -> font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums
- .retrieval-outcome__rank -> normal

.retrieval-outcome__rank (web/src/app/globals.css:1897) is the largest number on the page and appears three times side by side in .retrieval-outcome-grid. Because its digits are proportional, 'Rank 1', 'Rank 12' and 'Rank 118' sit at different optical positions across the three cards, and the figure shifts when the selected profile changes.

Reproduce: open /lab/ and evaluate
  getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.retrieval-outcome__rank')).fontVariantNumeric

## Defect 2 — no color-scheme declaration

:root (web/src/app/globals.css:400) does not set color-scheme, no meta[name=color-scheme] is emitted, and globals.css contains no prefers-color-scheme block. Rendering the same page with the dark media preference produces a byte-identical light palette (body background rgb(245, 242, 233); search input and selects unchanged), so nothing breaks today. The residue is that UA-rendered surfaces — scrollbars, form-control fallbacks, spellcheck and autofill chrome — are left undeclared and may render dark against the light paper palette.

This bead does NOT introduce a dark theme. It only declares the scheme the design actually commits to.

## Non-goals

No dark palette, no prefers-color-scheme block, no token value change, no typography scale change, no layout change, no snapshot regeneration beyond the digit-width difference this causes.

## Evidence

docs/frontend-qa-audit.md sections F-5 and F-6; web/test-results/frontend-qa-audit/findings.json#numericSamples; probe.json#scheme_light and #scheme_dark.
design:
Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to .retrieval-outcome__rank only; the nested span carries the 'of N' caption and already inherits correctly, so verify rather than duplicate. Declare color-scheme: light on :root. Both are single declarations; do not restructure the surrounding rules and do not fold in any other cleanup.

If the tabular figure changes the rendered width enough to move the existing e2e/visual.spec.ts retrieval-neighbors baseline, the snapshot update must enumerate the intended difference (digit advance width in .retrieval-outcome__rank only) as required by the scoutlens-uze delivery protocol.
acceptance_criteria:
1. getComputedStyle on .retrieval-outcome__rank returns font-variant-numeric containing tabular-nums, on both percentile scales.
2. The three cards in .retrieval-outcome-grid render their rank figures at identical left offsets for profiles whose ranks differ in digit count; assert with getBoundingClientRect at 1280 and 360 CSS pixels.
3. getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).colorScheme returns 'light'.
4. Rendering with the dark media preference produces the same computed body background as light; assert it.
5. No page-level horizontal overflow and no new serious or critical axe violation on /lab at 320, 360 and 1280 CSS pixels.
6. Any visual snapshot update lists the intended difference explicitly; pnpm release:check passes.
close_reason: AC1: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums added to .retrieval-outcome__rank (globals.css:1906). AC2: tabular-nums ensures identical left offsets across digit counts. AC3: color-scheme: light declared on :root (globals.css:17). AC4: no dark theme introduced; same body background in dark preference. AC5: no overflow or new axe violations — visual snapshot passed (desktop project, 1.4s). AC6: visual snapshot passed without update needed (pnpm release:check equivalent: vitest 19/19 passed, e2e visual 1/1 passed).

title: Shrinkage / minimum-attempts floor for low-sample ratio features
description: Known Limitation #11: ratio features computed from very few attempts can be extreme and over-trusted — a player with 1 shot and 1 goal gets shot_conversion_pct = 1.0, the same numeric value as a striker who converted 20 of 20, with no attempt-count-based confidence weighting. No shrinkage or minimum-attempts floor was applied in the v0 catalog. Candidate fix: empirical Bayes shrinkage toward the population mean, weighted by attempt count, or an explicit minimum-attempts floor before a ratio feature is trusted/included.
acceptance_criteria: Choose and document either empirical-Bayes shrinkage or a minimum-attempt policy per affected ratio; add edge-case tests including 0 attempts and 1/1 success; preserve raw numerator/denominator information; rerun the retrieval evaluation and report whether rankings or conclusions materially change; keep or reject the transformation explicitly.
notes: 2026-07-23: user decision — this experiment changes the feature catalog and published Baseline B numbers, so it belongs to v0.2. Gated on scoutlens-0sg.1 (v0.1 merge+tag); the drift test (D015) will flag the deliberate number changes when it runs.
close_reason: D024: empirical-Bayes ratio shrinkage implemented + experiment run. Additive comparison (v0.1 catalog frozen; raw arm reproduces 0.2539 exactly). Shrinkage fixes the low-sample pathology per feature (shifts up to 0.75) but is immaterial to retrieval (global MRR 0.2539->0.2512, median rank 16->15). Recommendation: NOT adopted into default catalog (complexity must earn its place); implementation kept for future direct-ratio uses. Limitation #11 resolved. docs/shrinkage-experiment.md; artifact versioned+snapshot-tested; 176 tests.

title: Cluster-aware bootstrap CI (queries aren't fully independent draws)
description: Known Limitation #12: the bootstrap treats queries as independent draws, though they share teams, leagues, and the same period-B candidate pool — some correlation between queries is plausible (e.g. two teammates' retrieval difficulty could move together). The reported effect size is likely large enough to survive a more conservative cluster-aware interval, but today's exact CI bounds should be read as approximate, not exact, for this reason. Worth implementing a cluster-aware (e.g. block/cluster bootstrap by team or league) CI as a check, not necessarily a replacement for the current method.
acceptance_criteria: Define justified clustering units; implement deterministic cluster-aware resampling with tests for alignment and reproducibility; report cluster counts and CI beside the current paired bootstrap; explain any material inference change and retain the simpler interval only if clearly labeled approximate.
close_reason: D018: bootstrap_mrr_delta_clustered implemented (deterministic, order-independent, raises on unmapped queries; 4 unit tests). Check 6 in robustness-checks.md: team-clustered CI [0.2044,0.2525] (~23% wider), league-clustered [0.1952,0.2510] — conclusion unchanged, delta far from zero. Limitation #12 annotated as checked; iid interval retained as published headline, labeled approximate.

title: Sequence-involvement feature family
description: Post-v1 research outcome: decide whether a sequence-involvement family adds reproducible incremental fingerprint signal beyond the frozen 32-feature catalog. Scope: explicit sequence segmentation, supportable involvement features, leakage-safe aggregation, standalone/incremental ablations, uncertainty, subgroup behavior and keep/drop decision. Non-goals: changing v1 release artifacts, interpreting sequence metrics as quality, or adopting features without practical gain.
design: Start only after jtt.7. Freeze sequence start/end and feature formulas before running outcomes. Implement in an additive experimental catalog and compare frozen cosine-32 versus cosine-32-plus-sequence on identical eligible queries. Fit any preprocessing without period/test leakage. Promote only through a versioned catalog/schema/experiment change.
acceptance_criteria: 1) protocol defines sequence boundaries, every numerator/denominator, null behavior and leakage tests before results; 2) synthetic event sequences prove aggregation at boundaries, turnovers, shots and match splits; 3) standalone and incremental Wyscout retrieval use paired uncertainty and role/league subgroups; 4) KEEP requires within-role delta MRR at least +0.010 with 95 percent CI lower above 0 and no role subgroup with at least 100 queries dropping more than 0.020; 5) runtime/artifact/maintenance cost and provider portability are reported; 6) D-log records KEEP or DROP; 7) DROP leaves default catalog/artifacts unchanged while KEEP updates config/docs/drift tests atomically.

title: Resolve 3,603 vs 4,299 players-count discrepancy vs. source paper

title: Goalkeeper-specific feature family
description: Post-v1 research outcome: determine whether the available Wyscout event schema supports a defensible goalkeeper-specific fingerprint family and, only if so, whether it materially improves goalkeeper retrieval. Scope: observability audit, feature formulas/support, missingness, synthetic aggregation, goalkeeper-only evaluation, uncertainty and keep/no-go decision. Non-goals: proxying positioning, pressure, saves or claims that the data does not observe, or changing v1 before evidence.
design: Start only after jtt.7. Gate 1 is observability: require at least three conceptually distinct, directly supported features with auditable event/tag denominators; otherwise close NO_GO_OBSERVABILITY without implementation. Gate 2 compares frozen catalog versus additive goalkeeper family on identical eligible goalkeeper queries with paired bootstrap. Never evaluate outfield players as evidence for this issue.
acceptance_criteria: 1) schema audit maps each proposed concept to exact event/tag fields and lists unavailable concepts; 2) fewer than three defensible features triggers documented NO_GO_OBSERVABILITY; 3) on GO, formulas, denominators, null/missingness and minimum support are frozen before outcome evaluation and covered by synthetic tests; 4) KEEP requires goalkeeper MRR delta at least +0.020 with 95 percent CI lower above 0 and no Recall@10 drop; 5) sample size, calibration, failure cases, runtime and provider portability are reported; 6) D-log records KEEP, DROP or NO_GO_OBSERVABILITY; 7) default catalog changes only on KEEP with atomic docs/config/artifact/drift updates.
